### (2) New defects

**[MAJOR] ARCH7-1 — F199 lets the build choose the swatch-size range, but UJ10.1-b, -d and -f assume fixed sizes (prd:543 R7.2; jny:576, jny:578, jny:580).** Outside the architecture lens proper; it meets this round's bar.
- **What the row now says.** R7.2 reads "its default and range the build's choice, never below MIN_SWATCH_SIZE". F199 says "at or above 24 pt … you can tune them at the P2 build".
- **What the cases assume.**
  - UJ10.1-b asserts the smallest size "measures MIN_SWATCH_SIZE on a side", which is exactly 24 pt.
  - UJ10.1-d and UJ10.1-f set 48 pt, and -d's second run sets 56 pt.
- **A correct build that fails.**
  - Take a build whose range is 32–96 pt, or discrete sizes of 32, 64 and 96 pt. It conforms to R7.2.
  - It fails UJ10.1-b and cannot run UJ10.1-d or UJ10.1-f.
- **What goes unverified.** Those two cases are the only ones covering:
  - R7.1's per-collection "Grid" choice and that choice not surviving a close;
  - R7.2's written-nowhere size.
- **How it slipped.** The round-6 pass checked "R7.2 (F199) pairs with UJ10.1-a, -b and -d, unchanged" (R6F:1226) without re-reading the fixed sizes.
- **Mutation that shows it.** Set the build's size set to {32, 64, 96} pt. UJ10.1-b fails, and UJ10.1-d's Given cannot be established.
- **Fix (companion only, testability under F199, 0 body words):**
  - UJ10.1-b's Assert: "Every swatch measures the smallest size the build offers, no smaller than MIN_SWATCH_SIZE".
  - UJ10.1-d and UJ10.1-f: "48 pt" becomes "a size S the build offers above MIN_SWATCH_SIZE, other than the recorded size".
  - UJ10.1-d's "or to 56 pt where…" becomes "or another such size where the recorded size is S", and its byte read uses "the swatch size's text S".
  - Alternative (owner): narrow F199 to a range that includes MIN_SWATCH_SIZE through 56 pt.

**[MINOR] ARCH7-2 — F200's premise holds only for text in the main file. Replaced text in a log frame needs a log reset, which cannot run beside a held write.** Locations: DF:105 ("but a wipe"); DF:228 (R6.2a); DFF:619 (F58 (7)); CMF:1700 (F200's "It needs no write lock… the deadline stays exact"); ADRQ:22 ("never holding a write"). CM R8.8 inherits the rule.
- **The scenario.**
  - An outside read R is running.
  - The user sets ZX-001's Swatch Name from Sky Blue to Harbour, then to Harbor. Harbour now exists only in a -wal frame, because R kept that frame from being copied into the main file.
  - The user fires "Delete selected". That is an R8.1g write, lasting up to DELETE_WRITE_BUDGET, and held indefinitely in a test build.
  - R ends.
- **What happens.**
  - A passive checkpoint copies both edits into the main file beside the writer, so Sky Blue goes. F200 holds for that text.
  - Harbour stays in its -wal frame until the log is reset.
  - A RESTART or TRUNCATE checkpoint waits for the active writer and briefly bars new writers.
  - So Harbour outlives R by the held write's remaining time, and resetting the log does hold a write for a moment.
- **Why it is Minor.**
  - No case fails: DJ3:47 is scoped to "a checkpointed file whose removed text is in no WAL frame", and F58 (7) leaves the reset to ADR-0003.
  - In production the slip is bounded by DELETE_WRITE_BUDGET.
- **Whose premise.** This corrects my own round-6 ARCH6-N2 premise ("a passive copy needs no writer lock"), which F200's Authority repeats.
- **Fix (0 body words; post-lock, owner-ratified because F200 is settled).** Add a post-lock § ADR-0003 item and a dated Clarified line under F200 and DF F58 (7): "F200's exact deadline covers text in the main file; a copy of replaced text in a log frame goes once no read begun before the wipe and no write in progress needs that log — at the latest when a held write lands — and the log's reset may briefly hold a write."

**[MINOR] ARCH7-3 — Putting the re-read into R1.11 (F191) gave it the exit clause written for writes (DF:105; DFJ:43–45; DF:329, OQ 13).**
- **What R1.11 now says.** "…or a re-read runs, … closing the file, switching and quitting wait for it, its progress showing, a failure cancelling them and staying up."
- **What the owner decided.** F191 (CMF:1642) settled only that edits wait.
- **What the grammar adds.**
  - Quit, close and switch now wait on a read that could be cancelled with nothing lost.
  - DF OQ 13 calls the fuller check superlinear at ceiling, so that wait can be long.
- **Where a builder guesses.** What is a re-read "failure"? A re-read that finds damage or a newer format lands in a file-opening state. Does that cancel the pending quit?
- **Coverage.** No case asserts either point. DFJ:44 and DFJ:45 say "each of those writes", which by its own word leaves the re-read out.
- **Why it is Minor.** Both readings are data-safe.
- **Fix (post-lock, owner).** Either "closing, switching and quitting end a running re-read rather than wait for it", or keep the wait, define failure as "the re-read could not read the file", and add a DJ3 line.

**[MINOR] ARCH7-4 — UJ9.5-d's byte read ignores the export's own deferral (jny:549).**
- **The mechanism.**
  - The second run starts an export at each set's first sample and edits the exported collection while it runs.
  - That export's read began before the edit, so it defers the wipe as well (DF R6.2a, "this app's own included").
  - The 20 edits also replace values that earlier edits wrote. Because the held outside read keeps those values in log frames, their wipe is a log reset, and that reset also waits for the export's read.
- **The mismatch.**
  - The Assert reads the bytes "within 5 s of the read's release".
  - The Harness (jny:79) says a case running an export reads within 5 s of its end.
  - DJ4:73 was fixed to "the later of" for this same reason.
- **When a correct build fails.**
  - The last export starts at the 20th set's first sample.
  - It exports a 10,000-item collection with IMPORTED_COLUMNS_CEILING columns of 200-character values.
  - A build whose last export ends more than 5 s after the release fails the case.
- **Fix (0 body words).** "…within 5 s of the later of the read's release and the last export's end, a functional timeout…".

**[MINOR] ARCH7-5 — The moved-file post-lock item omits the orphaned log (PL:138; DF:228's "beside it"; R6F:350).**
- **The bookkeeping gap.** R6F:350 closes privacy's deferred item, "removed text in a WAL left under the old name", as carried by F197-2. The item's text states durability only.
- **What stock SQLite (unix VFS) does.**
  - After an outside move, a WAL connection keeps writing through the -wal and -shm files left under the old name.
  - `sqlite3PagerClose` skips its checkpoint-on-close and keeps the -wal once `databaseIsUnmoved` (`SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED`) reports the move.
- **The consequence.** DF R6.2a's byte rule covers only files "the app keeps beside it". Text written after the move and replaced before the app re-homes can therefore sit in the orphaned log indefinitely, outside every rule.
- **Fix (0 body words).** PL:138 adds "…and no journal or log the app kept beside the file under its old name is left holding its text".

**[NIT] ARCH7-N1 — DFJ:44 and DFJ:45 open with "each of those writes".** F191-3 inserted the re-read line (DFJ:43) between them and the line they point back to (DFJ:42). Fix: "each of the writes two lines up names", or move DFJ:43 after DFJ:45.

**[NIT] ARCH7-N2 — The open-file check is credited to the wrong row, and a help-docs line describes an impossible case.**
- jny:79 and ADRQ:22 credit DF R1.11 with the open-file check "ending before the file takes a write". R1.11 does not name that check. What makes it true is that the file opens only after R5.4's check (DF:173, R7.6b); cite those.
- F201 (2)'s help line (PL:164) reads "While … the open-file check runs, text you remove stays in the file". F195 rules out a removal during that check. What the check can hold is a wipe pending from an earlier session. Fix it when the help docs are written: "text you removed earlier".

**[NIT] ARCH7-N3 — DJ4:72's deferral half can never be exercised on its declared fixture.**
- That half is exercised only when the removed text sits in a log frame the second read keeps.
- On a seeded fixture, a correct build reports it "not exercised" on every run.
- Declaring that the Given's text was written by an edit made while the first read runs would make it exercisable. Otherwise it is permanent gate noise; the end-state assertion still carries the line.

## Biggest risks
- **ARCH7-1** is the only item that fails a correct build. It is companion-only and should land before lock.
- **Fence wording keeps meeting WAL mechanics.** The deferred-wipe contract spans R6.2a, R1.11, E35/R7.6q, ADRQ:22 and the Harness. Each round's wording has run into WAL mechanics in a new sub-case: the later read (ARCH6-1), and now the held write (ARCH7-2). ADR-0003 should model the wipe as two mechanisms, each with its own blocking set:
  - the copy into the main file, blocked by readers whose snapshot predates it;
  - the log reset, blocked by any reader using the log and by an active writer.
- **Moving the file while it is open** is now a supported, tested path. Stock SQLite loses writes there on a clean quit, not only on a crash (see Genuinely sound).

## Genuinely sound
- **F191 is the simplest correct answer to ARCH6-2.** With no overlap there is nothing to reconcile, the refresh cannot miss a write, and R4.7's "a re-read ends that history" cuts cleanly. No capture can be in flight during a re-read (R7.3c). A reviewer arguing for concurrency here would be adding complexity for nothing.
- **F200 is right for the tested case.** DJ3:47's fixture is exactly scoped, and a passive checkpoint wipes main-file text beside a held writer.
- **DJ3:39 and UJ9.7-i (d) are load-bearing.** My round-6 claim that "a clean close repairs this" was wrong. Stock SQLite deliberately skips checkpoint-on-close for a moved database, so the quit followed by a with-app-closed read in both cases is exactly what a naive build fails. Leaf is the case's non-removing write, and it sits only in the orphaned -wal. The cases force the app to notice the move, and the watcher that updates E34's ⟨path⟩ is the same one.
- **F192 (ADR-0005 stops every row)** matches AGENTS.md §7.
- **F196 is a two-way door.** ADR-0003's migration mechanism can absorb a later undo representation, and R1.7 stays stopped by OQ 10.
- **F189 closes a real P0 hole.** Flag (R4.9) leads to set aside, then Capture R8.16's review, then R8.3's re-scan, all P0, with history kept. The seam is paired on both sides (Capture R9.9 and F76; the obligation lines).
- **F190's per-file E35 is buildable.** It needs a wipe-pending marker kept in the file, which fits R1.1's "nothing kept outside the file".
- **F195 is benign.** The open-file check cannot overlap a removal. It can hold only an earlier session's pending wipe, for at most INTEGRITY_CHECK_BUDGET, which fits DJ4:68's 5 s.
- **DJ3:47's "WAL frame" wording is not a pre-decision of ADR-0003.** The non-waiting save in ADRQ:22 already entails WAL on SQLite.
- **No round-6 edit pre-decides ADR-0004, 0005, 0006 or 0007.**
  - The first-phase sibling list and UJ4.7-d's set-aside list are seam-neutral.
  - The storage paths and UJ9.7-i work under either sandbox model.
  - F198's per-PR Mac run is an interim, with device OQ 21 as its closer.
- **F197-3's post-lock note is the right weight** for R8.11 on a network volume.

  - It opens an outside read, lands a removing write, and holds a write transaction open on another connection. Then it ends the read.
  - **Text in the main file only (DJ3:47's fixture):**
    - PASSIVE on a third connection returns `(0,1,1)` in 0.09 ms, and the main file is clean while the write is still held.
    - A zero-wait TRUNCATE returns busy, `(1,1,1)`.
  - **Text in an earlier WAL frame:**
    - PASSIVE cleans the main file, but the `-wal` still holds the text (count 1).
    - TRUNCATE returns busy, `(1,2,2)`.
    - The text goes only after the held write commits.

### (2) New defects from the round-6 fixes

**[MINOR] PERF7-1 — DF DJ3's new re-read line (F191-3) brings back PERF6-3's trap**
- **Where:** dfjny:43. Nothing holds the re-read, because R8.10a (prd:594) holds only "a write" that DF R1.11 names.
- **Cost:** the checks take about 0.2–0.35 s warm and 0.4–0.6 s cold at ROWS_CEILING on the M1 Air (round-6 qc_probe: 63 ms per 446 MB warm on the M5 Max). Driving each of the three UI tries takes about 0.3–1 s.
- **What goes wrong:**
  - The guard covers only the first try.
  - The capture-start and move tries land after the checks end, where "once they end each is offered" passes them.
  - So a build that never disables those two during a re-read passes, and a fast, correct build mostly reports not exercised.
- **Fix, 0 body words:**
  - **(b), companion only:** run DJ3:43 on UJ9.5-b's FILE_ITEMS_CEILING file with the OS file cache purged before "Read it again" (the checks take an est. 4–6 s cold). Make each try its own run, and have a try made after the checks end report that try not exercised.
  - **(a), deterministic:** when F185's post-lock item moves the held-write grant into DF R7.2, word it "an operation the Data Foundation PRD's R1.11 names" (0 net words) and hold the re-read.

**[MINOR] PERF7-2 — UJ9.5-d's second run: "fire All items so that its first rows load while the edit lands" cannot happen, and no app-side long read overlaps a capture save**
- **Where:** jny:549. prd:409 (R1.10: the All items view offers no export) and prd:407 (R1.8: "Export collection" is on the collection surface).
- **Why it cannot happen:** the edit needs the exported collection's surface. By the time the edit lands, the All items view has been left, and its load has finished or been dropped.
- **What slips through:** a core that runs every statement through one connection. One rusqlite connection behind a mutex is the common shape under ADR-0001, and ADR-0005 owns that choice.
  - It queues the set's save behind an All items first-rows load of ≤ OPEN_COLLECTION_BUDGET, est. 0.9–2.4 s cold on the 8 GB Mac.
  - That breaks R8.11. The first run overlaps the save only with a Scale keystroke and header, at most twice BROWSE_RESPONSE_BUDGET.
- **Fix, journeys only:**
  - In the second run, fire "All items" just before each set's last Demo sample, then type the keystroke and fire the header in it. Demo pacing runs on the test clock (Capture R11.7), so the harness can deliver that last sample while the first rows load.
  - Keep the export and the edit at the first sample, and drop the "while the edit lands" clause.
  - A run whose first rows showed before the last sample arrived reports that half not exercised.

**[MINOR] PERF7-3 — UJ9.5-a's grid runs name no swatch size, and F199 lets the build pick the default and range**
- **Where:** jny:546 ("in R7's phase … both pagings in the grid … change the swatch size 200 times"); prd:543 (R7.2); prd:571 and prd:574 (R8.1b, R8.1e).
- **Numbers:**
  - On the M1 Air's 1440×900-pt display, a grid of about 1,200×700 pt shows ≈1,450 swatches at 24 pt, ≈360 at 48 pt and ≈90 at 96 pt.
  - The continuous scroll moves one screenful per 100 ms. At 24 pt that is ≈14,500 swatches a second, ≈240 per 60 Hz frame. Each is a colour-managed chip with a code label and up to nine marks. That is the heaviest frame load in this PRD.
  - A build with a large default passes R8.1e at 1/16 of that load.
- **Fix, journeys only:** run the grid workload and both pagings at MIN_SWATCH_SIZE. The 200 size changes alternate between the smallest and largest sizes the build offers.

**[MINOR] PERF7-4 — "The wipe needs no write lock" (F200, DF F58 (7)) is true only of the copy-back**
- **Where:** fen:1700; dffen:619 (7); adr:22 ("waiting at most until every read begun before that wipe has ended"); pl:127–138.
- **Measured (probe above):** where the removed text sits in an earlier WAL frame — for example, a value edited twice while an outside read runs — the wipe cannot finish beside a held write. Only the write's commit lets it go. That is up to BULK_WRITE_BUDGET or DELETE_WRITE_BUDGET, 2 s or 10 s, past adr:22's deadline.
- **The gap:** DF F58 (7) says it leaves the WAL's reset to ADR-0003, but neither the ADR-0003 row nor pl § ADR-0003 carries it.
- **Risks:**
  - A build that takes E35 down when the copy-back lands hides it with the text still in the `-wal`, and no case covers that.
  - A builder chasing "the deadline stays exact" might zero old WAL frames in place. That breaks WAL's cumulative frame checksums. Crash recovery would then stop at the zeroed frame and drop every later committed frame not yet copied back — data loss against DF R1.10.
- **DJ3:47 itself is sound** (measured).
- **Fix, 0 body words:** add a pl § ADR-0003 item: "Where a WAL frame holds removed text, its reset needs the write lock: the wipe and E35 follow any held write's end, at most its budget; E35 follows the bytes, not the copy-back; WAL frames are never overwritten in place (DF F58 (7), Collection Mode F200)."

**[NIT] PERF7-5 — DF DJ4's second-read line (dfjny:72)**
- **(i) The not-exercised half can never be exercised.** The second read began after the delete, so it cannot pin the old page. Round 6 measured this: `(1,5,5)`, with db=0 and wal=0 while that read was open. If the text is present during the second read, that is only the app's poll interval, which the clause calls "the second read's deferral."
- **(ii) The Assert can race.** "E35 is up whenever the removed text is still in the file's bytes" reads two things at two moments. If the bytes are read first, a wipe landing between the two reads fails a correct build.
- **Fix:** read E35 before the bytes, and drop the clause. Do not make the clause "pass" by holding off the copy-back while any reader exists.

**[NIT] PERF7-6 — the open-file check at FILE_ITEMS_CEILING**
- **Where:** pl:164 (F201's second help line); adr:22 (F195); df:173 and df:313 (R5.4 and M8, ROWS_CEILING only).
- **The conflict:** the help line says text removed while the open-file check runs stays until it finishes. Under F195 the check ends before the file takes any write, so that can never happen.
- **Why it matters:** the check is unbudgeted at FILE_ITEMS_CEILING, est. 4–6 s cold for about 12 GB. A builder trying to speed up that open could read the help line as permission to run the check behind the shown file.
- **Fix:** drop "or the open-file check" when the help docs are written. Extend pl:171 (OQ 1's timing item) with "and the open-file check on UJ9.5-b's file, cold".

## Biggest risks   (what degrades first as data/traffic grows)
1. **One connection for the whole core.** A core that runs every statement through one connection stalls capture saves behind the app's own long reads. Nothing catches it yet (PERF7-2).
2. **A WAL-frame wipe beside a held write.** It can make E35 come down too early, and it invites in-place zeroing of WAL frames (PERF7-4).
3. **Cold All items open on the 8 GB Mac.** Est. 0.9–2.4 s against 1 s; unchanged, and OQ 1's to measure.
4. **Grid paging at the smallest swatch size.** It is the heaviest frame load and is not timed (PERF7-3).
5. **Opening a FILE_ITEMS_CEILING file.** The check alone is est. 4–6 s cold, with no budget (PERF7-6).
6. **Ceiling delete under `secure_delete`.** It pushes about 1.2 GB of zeroed pages through the log, so it needs that much free space (unchanged).

## Genuinely efficient   (incl. where simple-and-fast-enough is right that a perf-zealot would wrongly flag)
- **UJ9.5-d's outside read.** It makes the save-behind-a-deferred-wipe overlap deterministic, and its recorded guard can fire.
- **DJ3:47 (F200) can be built.** The copy-back takes 0.09 ms while the write is held. The line also forces the checkpointer onto its own connection, which protects R8.11.
- **DJ4:73 holds on both branches.** A short read and a deferred read both pass.
- **F191's hold costs nothing on a hot path.** A re-read already cannot run during capture (DF R1.5), and the hold removes the question of a wipe racing the checks.
- **F195 puts the open-file check in the right class.**
- **F199's build-chosen range is fine.** The floor is the only bound that matters for performance, once the timing case uses it.
- **R4.9 at P0 costs nothing.** A Flag is one R8.1c write, already in UJ9.5-a's workload.
- **UJ9.5-g's new read of a copy of the file (R6-m4) is feasible.** "Declared full" is an induced state, and an APFS clone is instant.
- **The 5 s functional timeouts are consistent, and no latency constant was added.**

## Missing / over-engineered   (premature optimization)
- **Missing:** PERF7-1 through PERF7-6.
- **Not over-engineered:** the outside-read hold in a Release-configuration test build.
- **Cautions:**
  - Don't fix PERF7-4 by zeroing WAL frames in place.
  - Don't fix PERF7-5 by holding off checkpoints while any reader exists.
  - Add no new latency constant.

### (2) New defects from the round-6 fixes

**[MAJOR] PLAN7-1 — R7.2 and UJ10.1-b/-d/-f: F199's "range the build's choice" contradicts three grid cases**

- **Where:** prd:543 (R7.2 now reads "…its default and range the build's choice, never below MIN_SWATCH_SIZE…"); fences:1696 (F199: "the default and the range are the build's choice, at or above 24 pt").
- **The cases:** they still pin the range.
  - jny:576 (UJ10.1-b): "Set the swatch size as small as it goes → Every swatch measures MIN_SWATCH_SIZE on a side". This requires the range's floor to *equal* 24 pt.
  - jny:578 (UJ10.1-d) and jny:580 (UJ10.1-f): "set the swatch size to 48 pt" (and 56 pt). This requires the range to include 48 and 56 pt.
- **The slip:** fix6:780 says "UJ10.1-b and UJ10.1-d already read it". UJ10.1-b does not: it asserts equality with the floor, which R7.2 no longer states. The journeys' own rule applies: "a case never introduces a rule".
- **Mutation that fails a build R7.2 accepts:**
  - A continuous 32–96 pt control fails UJ10.1-b (32 ≠ 24).
  - Stepped sizes of 24/32/64 pt fail UJ10.1-d and UJ10.1-f (48 pt can't be set).
- **Scope:** R7.2 is P2 and pre-alignment, so no earlier phase stalls.
- **Fix (companion only, 0 body words, testability under F199):**
  - UJ10.1-b's Given records "the smallest size the build offers" before the case; its Assert becomes "every swatch measures that recorded size, which is no smaller than MIN_SWATCH_SIZE".
  - UJ10.1-d and UJ10.1-f replace "48 pt" (and UJ10.1-d's 56 pt branch) with "a size S the build offers, other than the recorded default, declared before the Given".
- **Owner alternative:** if the owner meant the range to *reach* MIN_SWATCH_SIZE, so that OQ 6's owner check can see 24 pt swatches in the P2 build, add a dated clarification on F199 and "from MIN_SWATCH_SIZE" to R7.2 (+2 words; there is room). UJ10.1-d/f's 48 pt would still need the same companion fix.

## Biggest risks (if executed as-is)
1. **PLAN7-1.** A P2 build that follows F199 literally fails the grid cases. Nothing earlier stalls.
2. **Cross-PRD gating is now written down, but it is transitive.** The first phase waits on capture's P0, which includes R10.6's ADR-0004 prototype. The last Build dependencies row's "no row here" understates this: R1.5's "Go to the session" and the session-driven cases reach it through capture. Nothing is wrong in this PRD; the order is just long.
3. **The DF and Collection Mode test seams depend on each other.** DF's DJ3/DJ4 lines cite Collection Mode R8.10a, and this PRD's first phase runs on DF's P0. The two first phases must be built together (F185 settled where the seam lives).

## User & problem context (brief)
- **User and job.** The primary user is the Cataloger; the secondary users are the Data consumer and the QC re-checker. After a capture session they want to browse honestly, fix a bad scan without losing its history (vision U5), and keep metadata tidy while other tools read the file.
- **Validated vs assumed.** F1–F201 are owner decisions. Everything else is assumed, and dogfooding is the only feedback loop, which is the right size for a one-user open-source tool.
- **What I read, at d248158.** The four targets; the round-7 fix file; my round-7 section and the round-7 verify table in the review log; F199 in the fences file; the Data Foundation (DF) PRD's R1.11, R2.9 and R6.2a, and its E35 copy; the capture PRD's R5.6, R8.3, R8.16, R9.9 and R11.11; post-lock.md; and the full `git diff a720dae HEAD -- docs ':!docs/agent-reviews'`, word-diffed.

### (2) New defects from the round-7 fixes

No new Blocker or Major.

**[MINOR] UJ10.1-d's "the recorded size" can mean two sizes** (JRN:578).
- **Why it's ambiguous.** The Given records the default size ("recorded before the Given"). A1 then added "S recorded" to the When. Both halves of the Assert still say "its swatches show at the recorded size", which now has two candidates.
- **Why it's only Minor.** The intended reading (the default) follows from R7.2 ("lasts while the file stays open") and R8.6 ("saved window state included"). It also follows from the Assert's own first clause ("Neither read holds S's number") and from "shows as the table" in the same sentence. A builder who read it as S would write a test that contradicts both rows, so nobody has to guess.
- **Fix (journeys only, 0 body words).** Change both occurrences to "at the size recorded before the Given", which is the fix box's own wording (round-7 fixes:27).

**[NIT] UJ10.1-d can't run if every size the build offers collides with a seeded number** (JRN:578).
- An example is a build offering only 32 pt and 48 pt: Gouache ZX-001 has C* 32 and ZX-005 has L* 48.
- The case has no "not exercised" clause for this. It's very unlikely at P2, and the Harness's exemption and baseline rules already cover the collision. Post-lock, or ignore.

**Product views on the items round 7 left for my lens** (all Minor, all already routed to post-lock):
- **7N1: quit waits for a re-read** (DF R1.11; now asserted by DF DJ3's close, switch and quit runs, DF journeys:45; C3 at PL:43).
  - *Scenario.* The Cataloger fires "Read it again" on a large file, then quits. Quit blocks for a length of time nothing bounds, with no cancel, on an operation that writes nothing.
  - *Recommendation.* Closing, switching and quitting should cancel the re-read. Nothing is lost, because writes are held during the re-read and the next open runs the open-file check anyway.
  - *Why it doesn't block lock.* The case matches the row as it stands, and both change together if the owner flips it.
- **E35 during a wipe held up by a write in progress** (C1, PL:144).
  - *Scenario.* The other app's read has ended, but a long write is still running. Replaced text left in the file's write-ahead log waits for that write to finish, so E35 briefly says "another app is reading your file" when none is.
  - *Recommendation.* The window lasts seconds, and it needs an outside reader, a removal and a long write all at once. Watch it in dogfooding; no change before lock.
- **F201 (2)'s help line** (PL:172). I prefer one line covering both cases, in the user's words: "If another app, an export or Save a copy is reading your file when you remove or replace text, SpectroCapture wipes the old text once that read finishes, or when you next open the file." This is the owner's call at the help-docs pass.

**False positives checked, not raised:**
- **UJ4.7-d vs UJ4.5-b's later phase.** UJ4.7-d re-scans an unsettled set-aside row through capture R8.3, which is P0. UJ4.5-b depends on the capture PRD's later re-scan rows (P1). They are different rows, so there is no phase conflict.
- **UJ10.1-d's reset at reopen.** It extends to the size the table reset that R7.1's half of the case has asserted for several rounds, and it reads R7.2's own "lasts while the file stays open".
- **PRD body edits.** B12 (Rows cells) and B13 (word-neutral) change indexes only. The status flips match the round-7 flip record exactly: 118 aligned, with R7.1, R7.2, R8.6 and R8.8 held.
- **The byte-check fixes.** UJ9.5-a, UJ9.5-d and A3's raw-file baseline are test, performance and privacy mechanics. None changes what the user gets.

## Biggest risks   (what builds the wrong thing or fails the user)
1. **Density vs smoothness in the grid is decided at the P2 tuning, not in the PRD.** F199 lets the build choose its range, and UJ9.5-a now times the grid at the smallest size the build offers. A build that drops frames at 24 pt can therefore pass by raising its minimum. That is F199 working as intended, because the owner tunes it on their own display, but the owner should know the trade is theirs to make at the P2 build.
2. **The P0 correction loop still depends on the capture PRD shipping its set-aside list and look-through re-scan in its own first phase.** UJ4.7-d now proves the loop end to end. The remaining risk is sequencing only: JRN:66 names both.

## Genuinely solid   (incl. where simplicity is right that a product-zealot would over-spec)
- **A1 is the minimal correct fix.** It changes only the cases, names no new constant, and needs two offered sizes rather than three, so it asks the build for nothing beyond R7.2.
- **B9 closes the U5 story in one case.** The Cataloger can Flag a bad scan at P0, re-scan it, and see both readings kept, with no correction question.
- **Round-7 items went to post-lock.** Items that need the owner (C3, C4) are marked "needs owner" there rather than decided in a fix pass, and no fence was edited.
- **No new row, state, metric or constant entered the PRD.** The body is at 11,986 of 12,000, which leaves room for the lock line. No ceremony was added: no metric, persona or funnel. That is right for a one-user local tool.

## Missing / over-specified
- **Missing (lock pass, 0 body words):** UJ10.1-d's "the size recorded before the Given" (the Minor above).
- **Missing (post-lock, pre-existing, one line):** nothing tests that each collection keeps its own swatch size. UJ10.1-f never shows Gouache Set as a grid, so a build with one global size passes.
- **Over-specified:** nothing new to cut.

### (2) New defects from the round-7 fixes
No Blocker or Major. The Minors and Nits, one line each:

- **[MINOR] 8MN1 — UJ10.1-d's file read now carries real weight, and the Harness gives it no guard against chance matches** (journeys:578, :89, :106–108).
  - Before this pass, 48 was held by a seeded value (ZX-005, L* 48), so the file read exempted it and the check was vacuous. A1's rule, "an S whose number no seeded value's text holds", removes that exemption.
  - The file's raw scan (journeys:89) is a substring match in UTF-8 and UTF-16 with no whole-token bound. The number baseline (journeys:106–108) covers only "the same storage". A chance run of S's digits in the seeded file's binary content, such as compressed sample archives or page data, therefore fails a correct build.
  - A build offering only sizes whose numbers are seeded, such as {32, 48} (Cerulean C* 32, Demo Red L* 48), cannot run the case at all.
  - **Fix:** "choosing an S whose number the seeded file's bytes hold nowhere, the case reporting not exercised where no offered size qualifies".
- **[MINOR] 8MN2 — A3's count baseline treats unrelated growth as a new write** (journeys:108).
  - A raw-read binary file in the app's storage that grows during the When, for example an appended shader or URL cache, gains chance two- or three-digit tokens. A correct build can then fail a number check.
  - A3 narrows R7-M2 but leaves this case. The test lens owns the rule.
- **[MINOR] 8MN3 — UJ9.5-d's "All items" half** (journeys:549).
  - Once "All items" is showing, the next set's "Export collection" is not offered there (R1.10: "no collection rename, delete or export"), and the When never returns to a collection. The gap is partly pre-existing.
  - "showed its first rows before each set's last Demo sample" does not say whether one set that overlaps is enough to count the half as exercised.
  - **Fix:**
    - "…at each set's first Demo sample, choose that collection, start an export…";
    - "…a run in which, in every set, 'All items' showed its first rows before that set's last Demo sample…".
- **[NIT] 8N1 — DF DJ3's re-read line may inherit UJ9.5-b's gating** (DF journeys:45). "As its UJ9.5-b declares it" can be read as also inheriting UJ9.5-b's "R1.9, R3.7 and R8.2 built", which would push a P0 DF R1.11 check into P1. Write "the file UJ9.5-b declares, nothing else of its Given".

The rule their storage half actually enforces for a collection name or an item value is DF R1.1 ("Nothing about a collection or session is kept elsewhere"), which UJ9.7-i already cites. R8.6's list covers view state, not content. The effect is traceability only.

## Genuinely sound
- **A1 is the minimal correct fix.** The swatch-grid cases now ask of the build only what R7.2 grants: two offered sizes and the floor. The reopen assertion in UJ10.1-d reads "lasts while the file stays open" the same way the pre-existing R7.1 half of that case already read the identical phrase. So it is consistent, not a new rule. I checked the counter-case: a build whose default is "the last size used this launch, held in memory" does not conform, because its size would outlive the file.
- **A2's export folder.** Declaring the export folder outside the case's folder is what keeps a correct build passing. The export legitimately holds the pre-edit value, and the byte check reads every file beside the file under test.
- **B7's reordering is sound.** Reading E35 before the bytes is the only order a correct build can show. Dropping the not-exercised clause is right, because this fixture can never exercise it.
- **B9 closes the P0 loop end to end with values the upstream actually states.** DF R2.9 gives a re-scan after a Flag "reason initial and no correction question". R4.9 and F77 give the flagged reading no never-true mark.
- **B3's DJ3 line is now exercisable,** with a large file and a cold cache, and it asserts the close, switch and quit waits that DF R1.11 states, including for a re-read.
- **False positives I checked and do not raise:**
  - UJ4.7-d's "its history holds 2 readings" names no readback. The Harness's closed-file SQL read supplies one, as for UJ4.7-a.
  - B13's word-neutral wording loosens nothing a builder needs.

**(2) New defects from the round-7 fixes**

**[MAJOR] R8-M1 — J:578, UJ10.1-d. The file half of "Neither read holds S's number as text" now fails a correct build.**
- **Why it fails:**
  - The file's reads match substrings. The raw scan (J:88–91) has no whole-token rule, and the SQL read "matches as the raw scan does" over every value, internal tables included (J:91–93).
  - The only exemption is a *declared* value containing the text (J:93–96).
  - The number baseline covers the app's storage only, not the file (J:106–108, "the same storage").
  - A1's "choosing an S whose number no seeded value's text holds" removes the one exemption. The check is therefore live over bytes and values the file holds that no case declares.
  - At `a720dae` this half was silently vacuous: "48" was exempt through ZX-005's L* 48, as my round-7 side note said. It now fails in the other direction.
- **A correct build that fails:** the file stores anything undeclared that holds S's digits as a substring. A synthetic simulation (scratchpad, not a real build):
  - 40 text-UUID keys contain "64" 98% of the time and "96" 99%.
  - Spectral means stored as decimal text (18 readings × 31 values) contain "64" 100% of the time and "128" 67%.
  - Pure binary compressed payloads (30 × 400 B) contain "64" about 11% of the time.
  - ISO timestamps with fractional seconds, or schema text such as `base64`, also hit.
- **This constrains an open decision:** the blob and derived-value schema is Open (AGENTS.md §3). No choice of S avoids the failure under a text representation. A build offering few sizes can also be left with no legal S at all (for example {32, 48}: C* 32 and L* 48 are both seeded).
- **Fix (companion only, 0 body words), in UJ9.4-b's existing form:**
  - **When:** drop ", choosing an S whose number no seeded value's text holds", and read "…close the file, read the app's own storage and read the file at SQLITE_READER_FLOOR, then reopen…".
  - **Assert:** "The storage read holds S's number as text nowhere, and every table of the file holds the same rows as the seeded file read before launch, SQLite's own statistics tables aside; after reopening…"
  - A size written into the file then changes a row and is caught. Random digits cannot fail the case. The storage read keeps its number baseline, and the reopen and relaunch assertions are unchanged.

**[MINOR] R8-m1 — J:106–108: the count baseline does not cover a raw-read storage file the When creates or grows.** An example is a GPU shader or framework cache written as the file closes. By chance it holds a bounded two-digit S at about 9 per MB of new high-entropy bytes; this is analytic and depends on whether any cache grows during that When. Fix for post-lock: a match found only in a raw-read file counts only if a rerun with another offered size S′ matches S′ there too, since a real write follows the chosen size and chance does not. Or prefer a three-digit S where the build offers one.

**[MINOR] R8-m2 — J:576, UJ10.1-b: "read through R8.10b" ties each swatch's measure to the app's own reported size.** R8.10b (PRD:595) lists one "swatch size" per surface, not the geometry of each swatch. A build that reports 24 pt but lays swatches out smaller passes. UJ10.1-a has the same unstated measuring route, so this predates the round. Fix for post-lock: state that each swatch's on-screen frame is what gets measured.

**[MINOR] R8-m3 — J:580, UJ10.1-f: a single app-wide swatch size passes.** Gouache Set is never shown as a grid, so R7.2's "each collection's swatch size" is not told apart from one global size. This predates the round. Fix for post-lock: after choosing Gouache Set, fire "Grid" and assert its swatches are not S. Its fresh-launch size is recorded, and S is chosen to differ from it.

**[NIT] R8-n1 — J:602:** the storage line in the Test-controls map still reads only "a number against a baseline at the same key path". Fix: add "…and, for a raw-read file, by count".

**[NIT] R8-n2 — J:107–108:** "does not count only where …; and, in a file read as its raw contents, where …" can be read as requiring both conditions. Fix: "…in the same file, or, in a file read as its raw contents, where…".

## Biggest risks   (what could ship broken behind a green suite)
- **UJ10.1-d:** a correct build fails because of how it stores its data, not because of the swatch size. That pushes a builder to delete the file half, which leaves R7.2 and R8.6's "never written to the file" for the size unchecked (R8-M1).
- **UJ10.1-d's storage read:** it could fail now and then through cache growth, and a waved-away flake hides a real write (R8-m1).
- **Per-collection size and swatch geometry:** both are unproven at P2 (R8-m2, R8-m3).

## Genuinely solid   (incl. where minimal scoping is correct that a coverage-zealot would wrongly flag)
- **UJ10.1-d's "recorded size" oracle** is taken from the build, but that is not a fixture copied from the code. F199 leaves the default to the build, and the case uses it as a before-and-after oracle across a close and a relaunch. Where the spec defers the value, that is the right design.
- **The reopen check (R7-m1's fix)** fails the in-memory-map mutation: after reopening, "Grid" must show the recorded size, not S.
- **B9's "reason initial … no correction question"** matches DF R2.9 word for word, so it fails both of the plausible wrong builds. UJ4.7-d's run from the state UJ4.7-a left is allowed by the UJ 4 preamble.
- **B7 is correct.** In WAL mode, a reader begun after the delete commits does not pin the pages from before the delete. The dropped not-exercised clause could therefore never be exercised on that fixture. Reading E35 before the bytes removes the only order that could fail a correct build.
- **A2's deadline composes correctly** as the later of two deferring reads. The export goes to a folder outside the case's folder, so the old values in it cannot leak into "every file beside it".
- **B3's close, switch and quit runs** match DF R1.11. Leaving the "should they wait at all" question to C3 is the right split.

  - Row equality in place of the number scan for UJ10.1-d's file read (R8-M1).
  - A way to tell chance from a real write in raw-read files that grow (R8-m1).
  - Per-swatch geometry (R8-m2).
  - A per-collection size check (R8-m3).
- **Over-tested:** nothing.

## Genuinely well-designed   (incl. where a deliberate inconsistency is correct that a style-checker would wrongly flag)
- **The "later of" deadline in UJ9.5-d matches DFJ:73's Save-a-copy line.** It reconciles the Harness's two read-moment rules (an export's end, and the moments a held outside read names) with no new Harness rule.
- **UJ10.1-d's reopen assertion checks R7.2's scoping.** It uses the row's own words, "lasts while the file stays open", and the recorded default is scoped per collection ("on Studio Markers"), which matches R7.2's "each collection's swatch size".
- **The "All items" half fails loudly when it cannot be exercised.** A run where the load finished before the sample arrived reports "not exercised, never passed" rather than a quiet pass, which is the error model this surface wants.
- **B10 correctly left the ADR-0003 row alone.** Its cite already pairs the re-read with R1.11 and the open-file check with R5.4, so the change would not have been the same fix.
- **B13 chose word-neutral wording over a +3 literal fix, to stay inside the body cap.** "Multi-item selection" reuses R1.10's term rather than coining one.

#### peer-architecture-reviewer (Claude route)

## Verdict
**Sound: build it, after one more companion-only Major fix (ARCH8-1) before lock.** The round-7 pass resolves ARCH7-4 and every one of my Minors and Nits. It resolves ARCH7-1 only in part: the new rule for choosing S in UJ10.1-d makes the file-byte half of that case fail a correct build, and on some conforming builds makes the case impossible to run. There is no Blocker.

## Architecture in brief
- **The shape is unchanged.** Collection Mode browses and edits over Data Foundation's single SQLite file.
  - DF R1.11 holds writes while a write, commit, move or re-read runs.
  - A deferred wipe removes replaced text once every read begun before it has ended, this app's own export included.
  - F200 runs the wipe beside a held write. C1 now records the second mechanism (the log reset) for ADR-0003.
- **The round-7 diff is all companion-side, with no row rule changed.** It touches journey cases, Rows cells, one inherited-obligation Rows cell (B12), a Build-dependencies label (B13), DF journeys DJ3 and DJ4, DF R7.6q (word-neutral), post-lock items and Status cells.
- **The tradeoff is unchanged.** WAL on a local volume means capture never stalls, and the byte rule lands only once earlier reads end.

### (2) New defects from the round-7 fixes

**[MAJOR] ARCH8-1 — UJ10.1-d's file-byte check on S is now live, but the Harness gives the file no number baseline. A correct build fails it, and some conforming builds cannot run it (J:578, introduced by A1).**

*Why the check is now live.* Three things combine:
- The exemption for the file's bytes and the SQL read is keyed to values the case declares (J:94–96).
- The number baseline applies only to "the same storage", meaning the app's own storage, which R8.10e defines as "never the file's bytes" (J:106–108).
- Before A1, the size's text 48 was exempt because ZX-005 declares L* 48 (J:139). So the file half of the check was empty, but it could never fail. A1's S-choice clause removes that exemption on purpose.

*How a correct build fails (the mutation).*
- A build offers {32, 64, 96} pt with a default of 64. The case chooses S = 96, which no declared value holds.
- The build writes no size anywhere.
- To catch the real defect (a size stored as `96.0` in a REAL column), the SQL read must render numeric columns as decimal text (J:91–93). It checks "every word of the text whatever its length" in every table.
- DF R1.2 (DF:98) requires derived sets and decoded samples to be stored as plain SQLite types. That is hundreds of REALs across 18 readings that the case does not declare.
- Their text holds almost every two-digit string, and epoch-encoded time axes add more (2026-09-01T10:00Z is `1788256800`, which holds "88" and "56").
- So the file half fails almost deterministically.

*How a conforming build cannot run the case (the second mutation).*
- A build offers {24, 32, 48} pt with a default of 24. R7.2 and F199 allow this.
- S must then be 32 or 48. The seeded values hold 32 (Gouache ZX-001's C* 32 at J:149; ZX-001's u* −32.0 at J:135) and 48 (ZX-005's L* 48 at J:139). So no S qualifies.
- R7.1's "the choice does not survive a close or relaunch" and R7.2's "written nowhere" then lose their only case. This is ARCH7-1's failure again.

*Fix (companion only, 0 body words).*
- Drop the S-choice clause. S becomes any size the build offers other than the recorded one.
- The file half of the Assert becomes UJ9.4-b's form (J:542): "the app's own storage holds S's number nowhere, and the file read with the app closed at SQLITE_READER_FLOOR holds the same rows, table for table, as a read of it taken before the When, SQLite's own statistics tables aside".
- This is exact for an action that writes nothing. It catches a size written in any type and never trips on values the case does not declare.
- *Alternative:* extend the number baseline to the file's reads, by row and column for the SQL read and by count across the file and every file beside it for the raw scan. A per-file count fails, because a checkpoint at close copies pages from the -wal into the main file.

**[MINOR] ARCH8-2** — UJ10.1-d's reopen and relaunch assertions ("its swatches show at the recorded size", J:578) assume the default is one fixed size. F199 would allow a default that tracks window width, and a restored window can differ from a fresh launch's. Fix: record the size at the same window frame, or state that the default is per build. Post-lock.

**[MINOR] ARCH8-3** — A3's count baseline (J:108) covers a raw-read file that was present at the baseline. It does not cover one created or grown during the When: every bounded S in a new binary cache still counts. This is R7-M2's residual, and it is low-likelihood for this When (set a size, close the file). Post-lock, for the test lens.

**[MINOR] ARCH8-4** — C1's "the log's reset" (PL:144) should say truncation.
- A reset that does not truncate lets the next writer reuse the log from its start, leaving older frames past its end, replaced text included, until they are overwritten.
- Only a truncating reset (or a size limit that truncates) meets R6.2a's rule for "files it keeps beside it".
- This is ADR-0003 input wording. Post-lock.

**[NIT] ARCH8-N1** — The Harness's first-phase sibling list (J:63–67) names only the Data Export PRD's E1. UJ9.5-d's second run is now first-phase and completes exports whose rows it reads (Export R1.1, P0 there). The phase rule already allows this, so the gap is in the index only: add "and its R1.1".

## Biggest risks
- **ARCH8-1** is the only item that fails a correct build. It is companion-only, and it holds R7.1, R7.2 and R8.6 until it lands.
- **Byte checks on a number** are the one area the Harness cannot yet oracle cleanly. UJ10.1-d is the only case that needs one (J:578). For an action that writes nothing, checking that the rows are unchanged beats text-matching a number.

### (2) New defects from the round-7 fixes

**[MAJOR] PLAN8-1 — UJ10.1-d (jny:578): A1 took away the exemption that kept the file read from matching S's digits in undeclared bytes, and put nothing in its place**

- **Where:**
  - jny:578. The When says "choosing an S whose number no seeded value's text holds". The Assert says "Neither read holds S's number as text".
  - The Harness's file reads:
    - The raw scan is a plain match with no whole-token rule (jny:89–91). The test lens said so itself at round 7 (R7-m3), which is why qqq became qzxqvj.
    - The SQL read "matches as the raw scan does" across every table, internal tables included (jny:91–93).
    - The exemption covers only a word contained in a value "as the case declares that value" (jny:94–95).
  - The number baseline covers "the same storage", meaning the app's own storage (jny:106–108). The Test-controls map's line for the file (jny:601) gives it no baseline.
- **Before round 7:** ZX-005's declared L* 48 (jny:139) made "48" exempt, so the file half of this read was vacuous. The test lens's side note (R7-M2) offered two options: pick an S no seeded value holds, or leave the file read as it was. A1 took the first, which makes the check live.
- **Why a correct build fails:** S is a 2- or 3-digit number, and a continuous range makes 2 digits the natural pick. The seeded file holds many values no case declares:
  - the spectral samples behind each declared L*/C*/h°;
  - record times and archived payloads;
  - snapshot fields other than serial and firmware;
  - schema text, and any sqlite_stat1 rows.

  Neither way of reading those values rescues the case:
  - **If the SQL read renders numbers as text:** a value like 0.3712… contains "37", and a 400–700 nm band grid contains "40" to "70". Across roughly 2,000 band values a collision is close to certain.
  - **If they are BLOBs:** the raw scan sees high-entropy bytes, about one hit per 64 KB for a given 2-byte sequence, before the UTF-16 forms are counted.

  None of these values is exempt, and the harness text doesn't say which reading applies.
- **Mutation that fails wrongly:** take a build that keeps S only in memory, as R7.2 and R8.6 require. Give it a fixture whose spectra are stored as REALs, and let the builder pick S = 40. The SQL read finds "40" inside "400" or "0.4012", and UJ10.1-d fails. The builder then has to guess whether the build leaked S or the case matched noise.
- **Fix (companion only, 0 body words, testability):**
  - **(a) Case-local, preferred.** In UJ10.1-d's When, replace "whose number no seeded value's text holds" with "whose number the Harness's raw scan and SQL read of the seeded file, taken before the Given, find nowhere". This case makes no write to the file, so any later match is the build's.
  - **(b) Harness-level alternative.** Extend jny:106–108 to the file: "where the text is a number, the file's raw scan and SQL read are also compared with the same reads taken before the case's When, a match counting only where the text occurs more times than there."
- **Rows:** R7.2 and R8.6, the rows carrying the written-nowhere clause that the S read checks. R7.1's assertions in this case are unaffected, because since round 6 its grid choice is checked by the relaunch, not by a byte read.

**Minors and Nits** (one line each; post-lock or a companion edit):
- **[MINOR] PLAN8-2 — jny:578.** After the close and reopen, "its swatches show at the recorded size" assumes a fixed default. F199 lets the build tie the default to window width, and a reopened window can differ in width. Fix: pin the window's size in the Given.
- **[MINOR] PLAN8-3 — jny:549.** Two gaps in UJ9.5-d:
  - "showed its first rows before each set's last Demo sample" can be read as every set or as any one set. Fix: say "of every set".
  - Scale's samples per row are never declared. At 1 sample, the first and last Demo sample are the same sample, and the "All items" half's order can't be followed. Fix: declare 3, as Studio Markers has.
- **[MINOR] PLAN8-4 — post-lock:144 (C1).** The item qualifies F200's "the deadline stays exact" for text in a log frame (fix7:93 says so), but unlike post-lock:43 it carries no "needs owner" mark. An ADR-0003 author could read an owner fence as amended. Fix: prefix "needs owner (qualifies F200):".
- **[MINOR] PLAN8-5 — prd:283 and prd:756.** OQ 6's closer has the owner judge 24 pt at the P2 build. Under F199 the build's floor may sit above 24 pt, so the owner can't see 24 pt swatches in it. This is the owner alternative from round 7, left open. Fix (post-lock, OQ 6): the P2 build offers MIN_SWATCH_SIZE for that check.
- **[NIT] PLAN8-6 — jny:602.** The map's storage line still reads "a baseline at the same key path" and omits A3's raw-file count. Fix: add "or, read raw, by count".

## Findings
J = `/Users/vinnypasceri/Projects/.worktrees/spectro-capture-collection-mode/docs/product/collection-mode/prd-collection-mode-journeys.md`

**(1) R8-M1: RESOLVED, J:578.**
- **What changed:**
  - The S-choice clause is gone. S is "another size S the build offers".
  - The Given ends "the Harness's SQL read of the file taken".
  - The When takes that read again after the close.
  - The Assert reads "the same rows, table for table … SQLite's own statistics tables aside". This is UJ9.4-b's form (J:542).
- **Can a correct build now fail it?** The file half: no, apart from R9-m1 below.
  - Row equality has no substring or number semantics, so undeclared REALs, text UUIDs, spectral text and timestamps cannot match.
  - The checkpoint at close moves pages between the log and the main file, but it does not change rows.
  - The check is no stricter than UJ9.4-b, a P0 first-phase case that already requires launch → browse → close to change no row. A build that passes UJ9.4-b's close path cannot fail this half through its close.
  - A synthetic SQLite 3.53.4 simulation backs this up (scratchpad only, not a real build). The file was in WAL mode, with text-UUID keys, REAL L*/C*/h°, spectra stored as decimal text and an FTS5 index. The first snapshot was taken with the app connection open and frames still in the log, then ANALYZE, `PRAGMA optimize` and close ran. Results:
    - **Correct close:** rows equal, bytes differ. This confirms that a byte count would have failed (ARCH8-1).
    - **A write of the same value:** rows equal.
- **Does a build that writes the size still fail it?** Yes, on every realistic route:
  - **The file:** a column, a new row or a new table changes rows or schema rows. A write still in the log is caught too, because the Harness copies every file beside the database before the SQL read (J:88).
  - **A sidecar file:** it falls under the app's own storage ("every other path its processes create or write", J:602) and is decoded there.
  - **Preferences, or an in-memory cache per file:** the reopen assert catches either.
  - **`@SceneStorage` or restorable window state that is restored:** the relaunch assert catches it.
  - **Any write that lands before the storage read:** the new value at its key path counts, because the baseline held only the default there.
  - **What slips through:** a size written only at quit and never read back (R9-m3), and a write removed again before the close (R9-n1).

**(2) B2: RESOLVED, J:378.**
- **"Neither raising the Data Foundation PRD's E11 nor entering its E26 (its R2.9)" belongs to "the new one".** This matches that PRD's own wording: "initial recovery never raises E11 or enters E26" (DF journeys:29).
- **A correct build passes.** After the one-row R8.3 acquisition, it may show an E11 naming ZX-013 (DF R2.4) and an E26 at ⟨n⟩ 1 (DF R2.8). Neither of those belongs to ZX-001's new reading.
- **Every wrong build fails:**
  - A correction-unconfirmed reason fails "reason initial".
  - An E11 for ZX-001 fails through its ⟨code⟩ token (DF copy:39).
  - ZX-001 in the unanswered set makes E26's ⟨n⟩ read 2.
  - Promoting the flagged reading fails "the new one current".
  - A never-true mark on the flagged reading fails its own clause.

**(3) New Blocker or Major in the round-8 diff: none.**
- **B1 (UJ9.5-d):**
  - Three samples per row makes the first and last samples distinct.
  - Choosing the exported collection first is required by "Export collection" anyway.
  - "In every set … reports that half not exercised" is the correct condition: the half is not exercised only if the overlap never happened.
- **B3 to B7:** cites and index only. The baseline sentence now reads as alternatives, and the map mirrors the Harness.
- **C1 to C4:** post-lock items only.

**[MINOR] R9-m1 — J:578 and J:542: "SQLite's own statistics tables aside" does not say their rows in the schema table are set aside too.**
- **How a correct build fails:** I verified that on a file never analyzed before, `PRAGMA optimize` at close (SQLite's documented close-time advice) creates sqlite_stat1 and sqlite_stat4. That adds two rows to sqlite_schema, and the Harness's SQL read includes internal tables (J:92–93). Read literally, a correct build fails, unless the seed already holds those tables.
- **Why Minor:** the intent is plain, and UJ9.4-b, which runs in the first phase, hits the same point long before P2.
- **Fix:** "SQLite's own statistics tables, and their rows in its schema table, aside" in both cases. That is 0 body words.

**[MINOR] R9-m2 — J:101–102 and J:108: storage chance-matches in decoded entries that the When creates.**
- Two kinds of entry sit outside both the key-path baseline and C4's rerun, which is scoped to files read raw:
  - unified-log entries, which are read decoded;
  - a new window's restoration record.
- **Estimate (not measured):** if a builder counts a log entry's timestamp as part of the entry, a two-digit S under 60 matches a minute or second field in roughly 5–10% of runs.
- UJ10.1-d is the only case that looks for a number in storage.
- **Fix, post-lock:**
  - Widen C4 to "a file or decoded entry the When creates or grows".
  - State that a unified-log entry is read as its message.

**[MINOR] R9-m3 — J:578, second run: there is no decoded read after the quit.**
- The first run's storage read comes after the document window has closed, so that window's saved state is already gone.
- A size encoded into saved window state at quit, and not restored, therefore passes. R8.6 names saved window state, and the Harness says a relaunch readback goes "beside the decoded read, never in place of it" (J:108–109).
- **Why Minor:** the realistic route restores the state and fails the relaunch assert. Only a write-only leak, with no visible effect on the user, gets through.
- **Fix:** read the app's own storage after the quit and before the relaunch, against the same baseline.

**[NIT] R9-n1 — J:578:** a size written to the file and deleted before the close passes row equality. This is the accepted cost of not byte-scanning a number. If wanted, take a second SQL read after setting S, before the close.

**[NIT] R9-n2 — J:378:** the observable could be named: "E26, where it renders, reads ⟨n⟩ 1, and no E11 names ZX-001".

## Biggest risks   (what could ship broken behind a green suite)
- **A green UJ10.1-d cannot hide a size kept in the file.** The remaining false-green routes are a write-only leak at quit (R9-m3) and a write removed before the close (R9-n1). Neither has any effect the user can see.
- **The remaining false-fail risk is small.** It is the schema rows of the statistics tables (R9-m1) and rare matches in log entries (R9-m2). Either could push a builder to weaken the storage half, which is why both fixes are worth doing post-lock.
- **Carried from round 8, still open in post-lock C4:** the global-versus-per-collection size check (R8-m3) and measuring each swatch's own frame (R8-m2).

## Genuinely solid   (incl. where minimal scoping is correct that a coverage-zealot would wrongly flag)
- **Row equality is the right oracle:**
  - It is exact.
  - The checkpoint cannot move it.
  - It does not depend on how the file stores values, so it constrains nothing about the blob and derived-value schema, which is still Open.
  - Its "writes nothing, so any changed row is the build's" rationale rightly stays out of the cell.
- **Pinning the frame does two jobs.** It holds a width-dependent default steady (F199), and it keeps the frame values in the storage baseline at the same key paths.
- **The case keeps F199 and F71.** S is any offered size other than the default, and the default comes from the build. The size "lasts while open" (UJ10.1-f) and is "written nowhere" (this case).
- **B2 did not weaken UJ4.7-d.** Declining a flat "neither renders" was correct, because it would have failed a correct build on ZX-013.

## Missing / over-tested
- **Missing, all post-lock:**
  - the schema-row wording (R9-m1);
  - a decoded-entry rerun with another size S′ (R9-m2);
  - a storage read after the quit in the second run (R9-m3).
- **Over-tested:** nothing.

**Sound: lock it.** ARCH8-1 is resolved. On the file side, UJ10.1-d is now an exact oracle that a checkpoint cannot disturb, and the case runs on any build that offers two sizes. ARCH8-2, ARCH8-3, ARCH8-4 and ARCH8-N1 all landed. The round-8 diff adds no Blocker or Major. R7.1, R7.2 and R8.6 flip to ALIGN.

## Architecture in brief
- **Shape:** unchanged. Collection Mode browses and edits over Data Foundation's single SQLite file, with WAL on a local volume. Held writes follow DF R1.11. A deferred wipe runs beside a held write (F200), and ADR-0003 now carries its two mechanisms at PL:148.
- **Round-8 diff:** companion-side only. The PRD body, the fences and the copy are byte-identical, so no row's rule changed.
- **UJ10.1-d's oracle is now split three ways, one failure domain per read:**
  - **The file:** row equality against a SQL read taken before the When.
  - **The app's own storage:** a number match against a baseline read.
  - **Behaviour:** the reopen and the relaunch, with the window held at one frame.

### (1) My round-8 findings

| ID | Status | Evidence |

A default that tracks window width therefore gives the same size again. "The size recorded before the Given" gives "size" one referent. |

It is correctly flagged "needs owner (qualifies F200)", and no fence was edited. For record hygiene, see ARCH9-N1. |

**ARCH8-1: the file check (J:578)**
- The S-choice clause is gone; S is now "another size S the build offers".
- The file half reads "the file holds the same rows, table for table, as the Harness's SQL read of it taken before the When, SQLite's own statistics tables aside".

**Can a correct build now fail the case?** No.
- **The file half is a logical read, so page movement cannot disturb it.**
  - The pre-When copy includes every file beside the main file (J:87–88), so rows still in the log count in the baseline.
  - A checkpoint at close (log pages into the main file), deleting the log, or a vacuum that only moves pages changes nothing the read compares.
  - `PRAGMA optimize` at close writes only sqlite_stat1/sqlite_stat4, which are exempt.
- **Nothing in this When writes a row.** UJ9.4-b (J:542) already asserts that a whole open–browse–close session leaves every row unchanged, and that case is ALIGN. I checked Capture R11.16 and DF R6.5's activity and interaction records: they are capture-session-scoped, and no session runs here.
- **The storage half matches S's number only against the baseline** (J:106–108). The frame hold keeps AppKit's frame strings identical at the same key path. The only residual is a record the When adds (PL:98, ARCH9-3), and that item lands "at the next Collection Mode pass or the P2 build", before this P2 case first runs.
- **The behaviour half** is deterministic now that the frame is held.

**Can it run on any build that offers two sizes?** Yes.
- Any second size is a legal S.
- The {24, 32, 48} build takes S = 32 or 48.
- My {32, 64, 96} mutation takes S = 96, and a build that writes nothing now passes it.

### (2) New findings in the round-8 diff
No Blocker. No Major.

**[MINOR] ARCH9-1 — UJ10.1-d's baseline, the Grid choice's "written nowhere" (J:578).** The SQL baseline is taken after the Given has fired "Grid".
- **Failure scenario:** a build that writes the Grid or Table choice to the file when "Grid" fires passes the row equality. UJ10.1-d is the only case that fires "Grid" and reads the file, so R7.1's and R8.6's "written nowhere" for that choice has no file oracle. The reopen and relaunch checks catch only a choice that is written *and* restored.
- **Not new:** round 7's number match never covered it either.
- **Fix:** compare against the seeded file read before the case's first launch. That is UJ9.4-b's actual form ("the seeded file read before launch"). It also removes the case's reliance on a hot copy of a live WAL.
- **Keep the storage number baseline where it is,** just before the When. An earlier storage baseline would expose the number match to keys AppKit adds at launch.
- Post-lock, beside PL:96–98. It does not hold any row.

**[MINOR] ARCH9-2 — UJ10.1-d's second run, saved window state (J:578).**
- **Failure scenario:** run 1 reads storage after the file closes, and by then that window's restorable state is gone. Run 2 reads no storage at all after the quit, which is when AppKit writes the open window's restorable state. A build that encodes S into saved window state but never restores it passes, yet R8.6 names "saved window state included".
- **Fix:** in the second run, read the app's own storage after the quit and before the relaunch.
- Post-lock.

**[MINOR] ARCH9-3 — PL:98's rerun with S′ is scoped too narrowly.**
- **The gap:** it covers only "a raw-read storage file that the When creates or grows". Decoded records the When adds are equally outside the baseline: a new unified-log entry, a new key path, a new plist.
- **What a builder must guess:** J:101 does not say whether a decoded unified-log entry includes its timestamp. If it does, S = 32 matches any minute :32.
- **Fix:** widen PL:98 to "any storage record the When adds or grows". Also say that a unified-log entry is read as its message text.
- Post-lock.

**[NIT] ARCH9-N1 — record hygiene.**
- FX:59 (C1's Result) says ARCH8-4 "is not in this list and was not applied", but PL:148 carries it.
- PL:148's provenance also omits ARCH8-4.

**[NIT] ARCH9-N2 — PL:148's precision as ADR-0003 input.**
- **The truncation must reach the next writer's end or zero.** A `journal_size_limit` set above that point still leaves older frames between the writer's end and the limit.
- **"Log frames are never overwritten in place" holds only for committed frames.** SQLite does rewrite a frame in place when one transaction writes the same page twice.

**[NIT] ARCH9-N3 — B3's cite.** "(the Data Foundation PRD's R1.1)" on UJ1.3-c/e/f and UJ6.3-b cites only the app-storage half of the byte check. The file-bytes half is DF R6.2a, so write "its R1.1 and R6.2a" if the cite is meant to be complete.

**Checked, nothing found:**
- **B1 (UJ9.5-d):** "3 samples per row" makes a set's first and last Demo samples distinct, which the second run needs. Choosing the exported collection also resets away from "All items" in R1.9's phase. The not-exercised clause is now unambiguous.
- **B2 (UJ4.7-d):** "neither raising E11 nor entering E26" matches DF journeys:29. ZX-013's pending correction cannot trip it.
- **B4 and B5 (J:108, J:602):** the "or" makes the two exemptions alternatives, one per kind of read.
- **B6 (DF DJ3):** it now takes UJ9.5-b's file alone.
- **The C1–C4 post-lock items** are all consistent with it.

## Biggest risks
- **The grid choice and saved window state.** "Written nowhere" for them still rests on behaviour, so a write-only leak passes (ARCH9-1, ARCH9-2). Impact is low: the rows are P2, the data stays local, and nothing leaves the machine. The fix is post-lock at 0 body words.
- **Number matching in the app's storage** is still the Harness's weakest oracle. It is now confined to storage and to records the When adds (ARCH9-3); the file no longer uses it.
- **ADR-0003's wipe mechanics:** the ADR must pick a truncation that reaches the writer's end (ARCH9-N2), or replaced text persists past it in the log.

## Genuinely sound
- **Row equality is the right oracle for a When that writes nothing.**
  - It is exact and independent of type: 96, 96.0 and a BLOB-encoded size all show up as a changed row.
  - A checkpoint cannot disturb it.
  - It needs no knowledge of seeded values.

  A dogmatic reviewer might ask for the raw byte scan back "for defense in depth". Here that adds only false failures. Any size written into the file surfaces as a row change, and a sidecar file beside the main file is the app's own storage ("every other path its processes create or write", J:602), so it is still caught.
- **Holding the frame** is the minimal fix for a default that tracks window width, and it leaves F199's builder freedom intact.
- **PL:148** sits at the right weight: ADR-0003 input, needs-owner, qualifying F200, no fence edited. The truncation wording is technically correct.
- **B6** is good boundary hygiene: DF's case no longer inherits Collection Mode's R1.9, R3.7 and R8.2 gating.

## Missing / over-engineered
- **Missing before lock:** nothing.
- **Post-lock** (next Collection Mode pass or the P2 build): ARCH9-1, ARCH9-2 and ARCH9-3. N1–N3 can go at any pass.
- **Over-engineered:** nothing new.

**PLAN8-1 (jny:578).**
- **The file check is now row equality.** The Assert reads: "the file holds the same rows, table for table, as the Harness's SQL read of it taken before the When, SQLite's own statistics tables aside".
  - The case no longer reads the file for a substring. Undeclared REALs, BLOBs, schema text and statistics rows therefore can't match S.
  - A checkpoint at close moves pages, not rows, so ARCH8-1's objection to a byte count no longer applies.
- **S is any other offered size.** The case now says "another size S the build offers", with no condition on its digits. A build offering {24, 32, 48} pt has a legal S, and so does one with a continuous range.
- **Mutations.** My round-8 mutation (a build that keeps S in memory, REAL spectra, S = 40) now passes, as it should. A build that writes S or the grid choice into any row of the file fails. So R7.1's "written nowhere" clause now has a file oracle, which it lacked in round 8.
- **Answer to question 1: yes, with one exception.**
  - The only precondition is that the build offers two sizes. S, the default size and the window frame all come from the build, so an unattended P2 builder doesn't guess.
  - The exception is a correct build that keeps a row in the file only while the file is open (PLAN9-1).
  - The storage half still has its older risk of false matches in decoded reads (PLAN9-2). That won't stall a typical build.

**PLAN8-2.** The Given records "the window's frame at a fresh launch" and holds "every window the case shows … at that frame, the reopened and the relaunched one included". Both size clauses now read "at the size recorded before the Given".

**PLAN8-3.**
- The Given now reads "with 3 samples per row".
- The clause now reads "a run in which, in every set, 'All items' showed its first rows before that set's last Demo sample, reports that half not exercised". That means the half is skipped only if no set overlapped, the same logic as the export half's "no edit landed while an export ran".
- A side effect of B1: in the second run, the keystroke and header at each set's last sample now land in the exported collection (or in All items, in R1.9's phase), not in Scale. This is harmless:
  - R8.11 (prd:603) doesn't care which collection receives them.
  - R8.3 (prd:581) keeps the other collection's edit and export available.

**PLAN8-4.** PL:148 now starts "needs owner (qualifies F200):", in the same form as PL:43.

**PLAN8-5.** The OQ 6 item at PL:158 now carries the MIN_SWATCH_SIZE dependency. Both options stay the owner's choice, as F199's "tune them at the P2 build" allows.

**PLAN8-6.** jny:602 reads "a number against a baseline read before the When, at the same key path or, in a file read raw, by count". That matches jny:106–108, where B4 made the two exemptions alternatives.

### (2) New in the round-8 diff

**[MINOR] PLAN9-1 — jny:578, UJ10.1-d: the row baseline is taken while the file is open, so a correct build that keeps a row only while the file is open fails.**
- **Where.**
  - The Given ends "…the Harness's SQL read of the file taken". The app is running and the file is open at that point.
  - The Assert compares the read taken after the close against that baseline.
- **Why a correct build fails.**
  - No PRD or ADR says where the second-copy hold lives.
  - DF R1.5 (DF:103), DF R7.3d (DF:200), DF F13 and this PRD's R8.8 (prd:586: "because another copy of the app holds the file") all need a marker that another process can read and that a dead process can leave behind.
  - A row in the file, written at open and removed at close, is one legal place for it. So is an "open" flag used to detect crashes.
  - Such a build passes UJ9.4-b (jny:542) and UJ2.1-d (jny:258), because both compare the closed file with "the seeded file read before launch".
  - It fails UJ10.1-d every time: the baseline holds one more row than the read after the close. The P2 builder then has to guess whether to exempt that table or move the hold.
- **A second, smaller problem.** The baseline copy is made while the app is running, so it can race a build that checkpoints on an idle timer.
- **Fix (0 body words, Rows unchanged):**
  - In the Given, drop "the Harness's SQL read of the file taken".
  - In the When, write "take the Harness's SQL read of the file".
  - In the Assert, write "as the seeded file read before the case's launch". This is UJ9.4-b's own baseline.
  - UJ9.4-b is P0, so any build that reaches P2 already leaves the file's rows as seeded across an open and a close. This baseline therefore adds no new way for a correct build to fail.
- **Why Minor.** It only bites for one design choice, the same class as PLAN8-2, which round 8 graded Minor. It costs one clause, so land it before the flip, not after lock.

**One line each:**
- **[MINOR] PLAN9-2 — jny:106–108, jny:578, PL:98 (pre-existing since round 7's A3, not from this diff).** A number match is excused only by a baseline key path or a raw-file count. A decoded value that first appears during the When still counts if it holds S's number as a whole token, for example a unified-log entry, or a new plist key or database row that a framework writes at close. PL:98's rerun with a second size S′ covers raw-read files only. Fix: widen PL:98 to "a match with no baseline counterpart, decoded or raw".
- **[MINOR] PLAN9-3 — jny:578 (pre-existing test gaps; builds that break R7.2 or R8.6 slip through, and no correct build fails).** Three leaks escape unless the build reads them back:
  - the second run reads no storage after its quit, so a leak written at quit is missed;
  - the storage read looks only for S's point number, so a size index or name is missed;
  - S written into the file while it is open and cleared at close is missed by both reads.

  Fix: add post-lock items beside PL:96–98. They would read storage after the second run's quit, and compare an SQL read taken after setting S with one taken just before it.
- **[NIT] PLAN9-4 — jny:578.** "every window the case shows held at that frame" literally includes the Open panel ("open the file if the app has not") and any sheet or welcome window. Fix: "the window showing the file".
- **[NIT] PLAN9-5 — fix8:59 against PL:148.** C1's Result note says ARCH8-4 "was not applied". But PL:148 now reads "the log's truncation (a reset that does not truncate leaves older frames…)", which is ARCH8-4's fix. Correct the note, or log ARCH8-4 as landed, so the resume point isn't wrong.

**Checked, no new defect:**
- B2 (jny:378): the scoped form, "neither raising the Data Foundation PRD's E11 nor entering its E26", is right. "Neither renders" would fail a correct build through ZX-013's T3.
- B3: the four new R1.1 cites are correct.
- B6: DF journeys DJ3 now takes only UJ9.5-b's file.
- B7 (jny:68): Export R1.1 is P0 (`docs/product/export/prd-data-export.md:65`).
- C3: PL:45.
- C4: PL:96–98.
