## Findings

**(1) My round-14 Blockers and Majors**

| Finding | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|
| SSE14-1: (h) inherited (c)'s "within 5 s of reopening" clause and set no floor on read 2 after the reopen | RESOLVED | DFJ:55. (h) is now self-contained: no "As (c)", and no reopen-deadline clause. Read 2 ends "no sooner than 10 s after the reopen", and the copy must be gone "within 5 s of read 2's end". A build that clears only at open now fails: read 2 still holds the log at the reopen, and if the build never retries, the copy outlives read 2's end + 5 s. A build that follows F215 passes, subject to SSE15-1. |

My round-14 Minor m1 is RESOLVED at DFJ:54: (g) counts from the failure, the volume still full, and room returns no sooner than 10 s later. Minor m2 went to post-lock's ADR-0003 no-busy-handler note. My Nits are resolved or have post-lock items.

**(2) New Blocker or Major introduced by the round-14 fixes**

[MAJOR] **SSE15-1 — DFJ:55 (h) dropped the clean-bytes gate its round-13 form inherited from (c). The crash can therefore come before a correct build has wiped the main file.**
- **Before.** Round-13 (h) read "As (c), …". (c) crashes only "once a look after read 1's end finds the file's own bytes clean, the write still held".
- **Now.** The When reads "end read 1; while the write is still held, begin read 2 …; release the write; once it has landed, read 2 still running, crash the app; read the file's own bytes; reopen".
  - Nothing ties the crash to the main-file wipe.
  - The Result still asserts "within 5 s of read 1's end … the file's own bytes hold the removed text nowhere, and before the reopen they still hold it nowhere".
  - (c) at DFJ:50 and (g) at DFJ:54 both keep the gate.
- **A correct build fails.**
  - The app cannot be told when another process's read ends, so it retries the wipe on a poll. Say it polls every 1 s, well inside the 5 s functional timeout every DJ3/DJ4 row allows.
  - The harness ends read 1 at t0, begins read 2 at about t0+50 ms, releases the write, sees it land and crashes at about t0+200 ms.
  - The main file still holds the text, since the delete's frames were never copied back. The byte read before the reopen finds it, and "before the reopen they still hold it nowhere" fails.
  - Under R6.2a and F57 (1), a crash before the wipe is legal: the wipe then runs "at the first open after".
- **The case also stops discriminating.** A wrong build that holds the main-file wipe until every outside read ends, read 2 included, fails in exactly the same way. The case then no longer separates F202/F58 (7)'s "wiped once every read begun before its wipe has ended" from waiting on later reads.
- **Fix, journeys only.** When: "…release the write; once it has landed and a look finds the file's own bytes clean, read 2 still running, crash the app; …". The Result's "within 5 s of read 1's end" already bounds that gate.

**Minors and Nits (post-lock, one line each)**
- [MINOR] **SSE15-m1 — DFJ:48–55.** The rewrite dropped (a)'s "while the write still runs" from the main-file deadline in every row. DFJ:47 still pins F200 and F58 (7)'s wipe beside a held write for the checkpointed fixture, so no build diverges. For the log-frame fixture, though, no row now asserts it. Restore the clause in (a).
- [MINOR] **SSE15-m2 — CMF:1731 and DFF:649.** Each new bookkeeping line says the fence's whole "Decision … superseded by F215's/F61's principle". Those Decisions also carry the main-file "whether or not a write is held" clause and E35's "until the text is in none of those bytes", which F215 and F61 do not restate.
  - Scope both lines to "the journal-or-log deadline", as the round-13 lines at CMF:1711 and DFF:634 do.
  - The new lines also say "at the first open at which that holds", while ADRQ:22 now says "at the first such moment after reopening" (ARCH14-6). Add a dated Clarified line under F215 and F61 so all four sources say the same thing.
- [MINOR] **SSE15-m3 — PL:46.** The annotation says "clearing needs no room". That holds only when nothing is left to copy back, which (g)'s gate guarantees.
  - A clearing that must first copy a landed write's pages into the main file can itself hit ENOSPC. An example is (e)'s first write landing under read 2, then the second write failing for want of room.
  - R6.2a names no retry trigger for that case.
  - Narrow the annotation to "a clearing with nothing left to copy", and keep the rest of the E15 half open.
- [MINOR] **SSE15-m4 — PL:183.** The Dogfood item cites DJ3 (h) for "a crash that discards a held write". The rebased (h) crashes after the write lands, so no case now exercises E35 saying "Your changes are saved" at a reopen after a lost held write with a read spanning the crash. Re-point the item to "dogfood only".
- [MINOR] **SSE15-m5 — DFJ:55.** "After the reopen … E35 is up at each look whose byte read finds the removed text beside the file" gives no grace after the open. A correct build that learns of read 2 from a busy clearing attempt shows E35 a beat after the first look. Anchor the check at "once the file's opening state is up".
- [MINOR] **SSE15-m6 — J:397–403 "with no label".** The accessibility row reads "the Compare slot's accessible text". A build that renders "From current" as a sibling element outside the slot's accessible element passes. Define the slot's text as everything rendered between the two chips. The test and product-marketing lenses own this.
- [NIT] **DFJ:51 (d).** "This row or the rows around it" should name (a)–(c) and (e)–(h).
- [NIT] **DFJ:54 (g).** It has no not-exercised guard for a run whose held write lands anyway, for example when a one-frame commit fits in slack at the end of the log's last block. Today that run would fail a correct build on "E15 renders". Add the case to (d).
- [NIT] **DFJ:50 and :54.** The (c) and (g) gates have no bound of their own, so a build that never wipes hangs the run instead of failing it. (a)'s deadline catches that build.
- [NIT] **DFJ:52–53.** (e) and (f) still say "As in (b) until the held write lands", despite the fix file's "removes the 'As (x)' inheritance". The reference covers When steps only, so it does no harm.
- [NIT] **Fix-file D4.** It says PL:148 "was left unedited", but `17de231` edits it (now PL:151) to "not yet aligned". The edit is correct; only the record is wrong.

## Clarifying questions for the author
1. In DJ3 (h), must the crash wait until a look finds the file's own bytes clean, as it must in (c) and (g)?
2. Was dropping "while the write still runs" from (a)'s main-file deadline intended?

6. After the reopen in (h), must E35 be up at the first look after the opening state shows, or within a stated timeout?
7. Does (d)'s "the rows around it" mean exactly (a)–(c) and (e)–(h)?

**(2) New Major from the round-14 fixes**

**[MAJOR] TR15-1 — DF journeys:55 (h): the crash is not gated on the main file being clean, yet the Result asserts the file's own bytes were clean before the reopen. A correct build fails whenever the harness is faster than the app's detection of read 1's end. (DJ3, R6.2a, R8.8's inherited half.)**
- **Where it came from.**
  - At `7328002`, (h) read "As (c), …", so it inherited (c)'s gate: "crash the app once a look after read 1's end finds the file's own bytes clean".
  - The rewrite moved the crash to "release the write; once it has landed, read 2 still running, crash the app" and did not carry the gate over. (c) (:50) and (g) (:54) both keep it.
  - (h)'s Result still asserts: "within 5 s of read 1's end, a functional timeout, the file's own bytes hold the removed text nowhere, and before the reopen they still hold it nowhere".
- **Why a correct build fails.**
  - R6.2a (DF PRD:228) wipes the main-file text "once that read has ended and the file is open". Its only bound in DJ3 is the 5 s functional timeout.
  - SQLite gives the app no signal when an outside read ends, so a correct build detects it by polling.
  - A harness that runs (h)'s Action at machine speed kills the app before its first poll. The pre-reopen byte read then finds the text in the main file.
  - R6.2a is not breached: the file is not open, and the reopened app would wipe the text.
- **Probe (probe_h4.py).**
  - Setup: the text is seeded in the main file and in a committed log frame, and the seeding byte read finds it beside the file. The app wipes by PASSIVE checkpoint on each poll.
  - Harness: end read 1, begin read 2, land the held write, SIGKILL the app at +0.05 s.
  - Poll every 1.0 s or 0.5 s: "main file holds text before reopen: True". Both polling rates are well inside the 5 s timeout, and both builds fail (h).
  - Poll every 0.05 s: the build passes. Pass or fail therefore depends on the build's polling rate against the harness's speed, not on correctness.
- **With the gate, (h) is buildable (probe_h5.py).**
  - The main file is clean at the crash (+0.84 s).
  - The log copy survives the crash and the reopen.
  - With no busy handler, TRUNCATE returns (1,3,2) while read 2 runs, and the copy stays.
  - After read 2 ends it returns (0,0,0) and the WAL is 0 bytes.
- **Mutation.** A correct 1 s-poll build fails (h) as written. No wrong build is caught by the missing gate, so this is a pure false-red on the case that verifies F58 (1) after a crash.
- **Fix (journeys only, no PRD words).** "(h) … release the write; once it has landed and a look finds the file's own bytes clean, read 2 still running, crash the app; …". This mirrors (c) and (g). The uncommitted worktree edit reads exactly this; re-verify it next round.

## Verdict
**Sound: build it once two things are fixed.** The round-14 fixes resolve both of my round-14 Majors. The fix pass also brings in two new Majors, and neither needs a word of PRD body text:
- **DJ3 (h)** now crashes the app without first waiting for the main-file wipe, so a correct build can fail it (ARCH15-1).
- **PL:46's new note** says full-volume clearing is settled. The storage cannot deliver that when committed frames not yet copied in would make the main file bigger (ARCH15-2). I proposed that note myself in round 14.

## Architecture in brief
- **Ownership has not changed.**
  - Data Foundation owns the file, the erase lifecycle, E35 and the one-writer rule (R1.11).
  - CM R8.8 hands the journal/log copy to DF R6.2a.
  - ADR-0003 owns the mechanism. ADRQ:22's crash clause now reads "the first such moment after reopening".
- **There are two deadlines.**
  - Text in the main file is wiped at the read-based deadline, alongside a held write (F200).
  - The log copy goes at the first moment, with the file open, that no read uses the log and no write runs. Clearing holds the next write only for its own copy and truncation (F212, F215, DF F61).
- **The tradeoff is unchanged.** Writes never wait on reads, the log copy trails behind them, and E35 tells the user.
  - WAL is forced by the ADR input's non-waiting save, not by these rows.
  - R5.4 is read-only logic over stored derived values.
- **What I reviewed.**
  - The subject is `17de231`, read with `git show` and `git diff 7328002 17de231`.
  - The working tree now has uncommitted edits beyond the subject (DFJ:48, DFJ:55, DF:228, ADRQ:22, citing F218/F62). I did not review them as the subject. They appear to address ARCH15-1, ARCH15-2, ARCH15-5 and ARCH15-10.
- **Probes.** Scratch files only, in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-vinnypasceri-Projects-spectro-capture/d4b2a2e5-4696-48c6-9516-d4cbad888739/scratchpad/round15/arch15-probe/` (`probe15_growth.py`, `probe15_h.py`, `app.py`).
  - Setup: SQLite 3.53.4, WAL, `secure_delete=ON`, `wal_autocheckpoint=0`, busy timeout 0, outside reads as read-only connections in another process, the crash as SIGKILL.
  - The full volume used 8 MB HFS+ and APFS images mounted in the scratchpad, detached afterwards.

### (2) New Majors from the round-14 fixes

**[MAJOR] ARCH15-1 — DF DJ3 (h) (DFJ:55): the crash is not gated on the main-file wipe, yet the Result asserts the file is clean before the reopen.**
- **What the row says.** The When crashes the app "once it has landed, read 2 still running". The Result asserts "within 5 s of read 1's end … the file's own bytes hold the removed text nowhere, and before the reopen they still hold it nowhere".
- **What went missing.** (c) (DFJ:50) and (g) (DFJ:54) each wait for "a look finds the file's own bytes clean" before the next step. The old (h) got that wait through "As (c)". The self-contained rewrite dropped it. My own ARCH14-1 fix text had the same gap.
- **Why a correct build fails.**
  - R6.2a's deadline is "once that read has ended and the file is open", and F57 (1) lets the app wipe "on its own or at the first open after".
  - Take a correct build that retries its wipe every 2 s, inside the 5 s functional timeout.
  - A harness that ends read 1, begins read 2, releases the write and crashes within about a second kills the app before the wipe runs. Nothing wipes a closed file.
  - So the byte read before the reopen finds the text. In one probe run the app's wipe had not run before the SIGKILL, and main page 4 still held the text before the reopen.
- **Change that exposes it.** Crash 0.5 s after read 1's end against a build that wipes at 2 s. That build meets R6.2a and F57 and fails (h).
- **Fix (journeys only).** "…once it has landed and a look finds the file's own bytes clean, read 2 still running, crash the app…".
  - PROBE: with that gate, the log still holds the text across the crash in both sub-cases, read 2 begun before and after the copy-in. TRUNCATE returns (1,3,2) at the landing, before the reopen and after it, and (0,0,0) only once read 2 ends. So (h) is still exercised.

**[MAJOR] ARCH15-2 — PL:46's new note closes a live storage failure case on a premise that is not generally true.**
- **The note.** "The journal-or-log copy under E15 is settled by F215 / DF F61, since clearing needs no room (DJ3 (g)); what stays open is a wipe or clearing that falls due while E34 is up."
- **When that premise fails.**
  - Clearing needs no room only when every committed frame is already in the main file, which is DJ3 (g)'s state.
  - It fails when committed frames not yet copied in would make the main file bigger. That is the normal state after captures or an import land while another app's read holds back the copy-in.
  - It is also how a long outside read fills a disk: the WAL keeps growing. A sync client reading the file is the obvious real case.
- **PROBE, growth case.**
  - Setup: read 1 held; a committed insert of about 1.2 MB; the delete lands; the volume is filled; read 1 ends. No read and no write remain, so this is F215's moment.
  - On both HFS+ and APFS, PASSIVE and TRUNCATE fail with "database or disk is full", and the `-wal` keeps the removed text.
  - Once room is restored, TRUNCATE returns (0,0,0).
  - Control without the growth: TRUNCATE returns (0,0,0) with the volume still full.
  - The main file's own bytes did come out clean, because pages are copied in ascending order and in place, even though the checkpoint reported failure.
- **Consequences.**
  - R6.2a's log clause, and R8.8 through it, name a moment the storage cannot meet here, and say nothing about what happens instead.
  - E15 need not be up, because no write of the app's failed. E35 stays up with a false "another app is reading" headline.
  - That was exactly PL:46's open question, and the record now calls it settled. I proposed this note in ARCH14-2, generalising from (g)'s state.
- **Where a builder has to guess.** The ADR-0003 author reads the case as closed, and the implementation hits SQLITE_FULL at F215's moment with no outcome and no state to show.
- **Change that exposes it.** Run DJ3 (g)'s fixture with committed growth pending before the volume fills: no build can meet "within 5 s of the failure".
- **Fix (no PRD words).** Re-scope PL:46 so the growth case stays open next to the E34 half:
  - "settled by F215/F61 where every committed frame is already in the file, the clearing then only a truncation (DJ3 (g)). Where frames not yet copied in would make the file bigger, a full volume stops the clearing until room returns, with or without E15 up (round-15 architecture probe). Settle when it then runs and which state shows."
  - Alternatively, take an owner line on R6.2a. The uncommitted working-tree text "within 5 s of room returning" reads like that; it is not reviewed here.
  - Then add a DJ3 (g) twin with growth pending.

### Minors and Nits (post-lock, one line each)
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-3 — PL:169's definition of "uses the log".**
  - The definition reads "a read uses the journal or log unless it began after the file had taken in every committed frame". Read with "every committed frame" fixed at the read's start, it lets a read escape that SQLite still counts.
  - PROBE `r2_after_copy`: read 2 began after the copy-in returned (0,2,2), yet it held the text in the log once the held write committed. Backfilling then needs an exclusive READ_LOCK(0).
  - Fix: add "and no write has committed since it began".
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-4 — the new Clarified lines at CMF:1731 and DFF:649 say "this fence's Decision" is superseded.**
  - F215 and F61 replace only the journal-or-log deadline (F215's Scope bullet).
  - The "whether or not a write is held" main-file half stands through F200 and DF F58 (7).
  - Fix: read "this fence's journal-or-log deadline".
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-5 — (a) (DFJ:48) dropped "while the write still runs" from its main-file clause, which the old (a) had.** DFJ:47 still pins F200, so no wrong build gets through the set.
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-6 — ARCH14-4 is now load-bearing.**
  - With the write landed, every correct run of (h) keeps the text beside the file across the reopen, so E35 at the reopen is tested in every run.
  - A rule of "blocked truncation means E35" passes (h) but breaks F211's "only when another app's read defers a wipe". That leaves ADR-0003 with an in-file marker for a pending wipe, which is a schema decision.
  - Decide it before the first build PR that runs (h) (PL:151).
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-7 — (h) (DFJ:55) never asserts that the landed held write is in the file after the reopen (R8.8).** A build that throws away the `-wal` at the reopen reports "not exercised" through (d) (DFJ:51) instead of failing. Add that assert.
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-8 — (g) now depends on truncation working on a full volume.**
  - R7.2's declared-full test hook has to behave like a real full volume: writes that allocate fail, while truncation and in-place overwrites succeed.
  - A shim that fails every write would fail a correct build. Record this in the engineering plan's test matrix.
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-9 — (b), (e), (f) and (h) (DFJ:49, 52, 53, 55) can begin read 2 before the main-file wipe.**
  - F57's Corrected line (DFF:616) permits such a read to defer the wipe, yet these rows require the file clean within 5 s of read 1's end.
  - SQLite never defers there, so no real build diverges.
  - Fix: gate read 2 on the clean look. This predates round 14.
- **[MINOR] ARCH15-10 — (h)'s "after the reopen" E35 check has no gate on the opening state (DFJ:55).**
  - Every run now reaches it, so a look taken while the file is still opening finds the text and no E35.
  - DJ4:77 uses the same "at the reopen" convention.
  - Fix: "once the file's opening state is up".
- **[NIT]** CMF:1731 and DFF:649 copy "after a crash at the first open at which that holds", while ADRQ:22 now reads "the first such moment after reopening". "F215 governs" makes this harmless.
- **[NIT]** PL:183's fourth dogfood window cites DJ3 (h) for "a crash that discards a held write". (h) now lands the write first, so no DJ3 run shows that window.
- **[NIT]** (d)'s "this row or the rows around it" (DFJ:51) should name (a)–(h).
- **[NIT]** (e) and (f) still begin "As in (b) until the held write lands" (DFJ:52–53). Only actions carry over and the Results are self-contained, so this is harmless, but it contradicts the fix file's claim that nothing is inherited.
- **[NIT] Carried.** ADRQ:22's "so capture saves never wait on another app's read" follows from the non-waiting save and F212, not from the short reads. It is not recorded in post-lock.

## Biggest risks
- **DJ3 gates R6.2a, and the first build phase builds against R6.2a (PL:151).** As committed, (h) can fail a correct build depending on the harness's timing (ARCH15-1).
- **The full-volume case is realistic and now recorded as settled (ARCH15-2).** A long outside read makes the WAL grow until the disk is full. The rows state no outcome for it, and no state is true to show.
- **How a pending wipe survives a crash is a schema-level one-way door in ADR-0003 (ARCH15-6).** Durability ordering, with F_FULLFSYNC before truncation, is still at PL:169.

## Genuinely sound
- **Writing DJ3 as eight self-contained rows removes the "As (x)" inheritance** that produced a Major in each of rounds 12–14. (b), (c), (e), (f) and (g) each check out against F215, F61 and WAL semantics.
- **(g) is right.** In its state the clearing is only a truncation, and truncation needs no room (probe control).
- **(h), rebased on a landed write, is exercised in every correct run, including read 2 begun after the copy-in.** A dogmatic review might ask for read 2 to be pinned before the copy-in. That is unnecessary: once a write commits, a reader on READ_LOCK(0) blocks backfill, so the log keeps the text either way.
- **ADRQ:22's crash clause now matches R6.2a's "the file open" and DJ3 (h).**
- **The rows stay storage-neutral.**
  - A rollback journal in DELETE or TRUNCATE mode meets the log clause trivially, and PERSIST is ADR-0003's to exclude.
  - In rollback mode DJ3 cannot even be set up, because the delete waits on read 1's SHARED lock. That is consistent with WAL being forced by the non-waiting save, not by these rows.
- **F200's exact main-file deadline survives a full volume.** The probe shows the page copy happens in place.
- **R5.4's copy trigger now matches the row and F207/F217, and UJ5.3-r's "spectral" and D50/2° fix is right.** Nothing there touches storage.
- **The rows stay at the right altitude.** They state behaviour, not checkpoint modes or reader slots.

## Missing / over-engineered
- **Missing:**
  - (h)'s wait for the main file to be clean (ARCH15-1);
  - PL:46 re-scoped, then an owner outcome and a DJ3 (g) twin with growth pending (ARCH15-2);
  - (h)'s durability assert (ARCH15-7);
  - ADR-0003's decision on how a pending wipe persists (ARCH15-6).
- **Over-engineered:** nothing new. Eight rows sharing one fixture is a presentation choice.

## Verdict
**Privacy-sound to ship. This is the round-15 delta, `7328002..17de231`.**
- PRIV14-1, the one High from round 14, is resolved exactly as proposed.
- The round-14 fixes bring in no new Critical or High.
- Three Lows go to post-lock. One of them corrects my own round-14 wording at PL:46, which a new probe shows overstated what clearing the log can do on a full volume.

## Data-flow & PII map (brief)
- **Data subjects:** the Cataloger, and anyone named in notes, swatch names, collection names or imported free text. None of it is special-category. The delta adds no personal field, no store and no egress.
- **Removed or replaced text survives in:**
  - **The main file:** until reads begun before the wipe have ended (R8.8, R6.2a).
  - **The log beside the file:** until the first moment, with the file open, that no read uses it and no write runs. After a crash, that is the first such moment after reopening (F215, DF F61, ADR input).
  - **Outside the promise:** R5.8's pre-upgrade copies, Save a copy, exports and backups.
- **Disclosure:** E35 shows for another app's read and stays up until the bytes are clean. The app's own reads hold the text silently (F211), so the help docs are the only disclosure there.
- **Readers of a log copy:** anything that reads raw bytes, such as a sync client, a snapshot or a copy of the folder.

**Lows and Info for post-lock**

[LOW] **PRIV15-1 — PL:46, "since clearing needs no room": my own round-14 wording, and it overgeneralizes from (g).**
- **Why (g) is a special case.** In (g) the copy back into the main file has already finished before the volume fills, so only the truncation is left, and truncation needs no room.
- **The probe.** SQLite 3.53.4, 8 MB HFS+ and APFS images, run inline with no script file; the images were deleted afterwards. The sequence:
  - Read 1 begins.
  - A committed 150 KB insert grows the database beyond the main file's end.
  - The delete lands, then the volume is filled.
  - Read 1 ends, with no write running.
- **Result, identical on both images:**
  - `wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` and `(TRUNCATE)` both return "database or disk is full".
  - The marker is in the main file nowhere: the main-file wipe landed, because that page lies inside the file's end.
  - The marker is still in the log.
  - After freeing room, TRUNCATE returns (0,0,0) and the log is clean.
- **Harm.** Removed text stays in the log for as long as the disk is full.
  - E35 does stay up, so the user is told the text remains. But its "another app is reading" is stale by then.
  - Its promise "then wipes it on its own" has no stated trigger once room returns.
  - Low likelihood; the data is not sensitive.
- **Fix.**
  - Keep PL:46's E15 half open for a clearing whose copy back must still grow the file.
  - Add to the ADR-0003 notes at PL:169 that the clearing is retried when room returns.
  - (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), storage limitation.)

[LOW] **PRIV15-2 — CMF:1731 and DFF:649 (new pointer lines).**
- **The problem.** Both say the whole of F202's and F59's Decision is superseded. But F215 and F61 replace only the deadline for the log copy (F215 Scope: "This replaces F211's list").
- **What they sweep in.** F202's and F59's main-file clause ("whether or not a write is held") and E35's "until the text is in none of those bytes" are not superseded. R8.8 cites F59 for that guarantee.
- **Why only Low.** The harm is latent: the rows still carry both guarantees, and DFJ:47 tests the main-file half.
- **Fix.** Scope both lines to "this fence's journal-or-log deadline", as the round-13 lines at CMF:1711, DFF:634 and DFF:664 are.

[LOW] **PRIV15-3 — PL:169, the ARCH14-4 note ("how a pending wipe survives a close or crash").**
- **The problem.** The note does not carry the settled constraint that nothing about E35's state is kept outside the file (DF F58 (1), R1.1).
- **Why it matters.**
  - The storage check for that constraint (PL:44) is still open, and no DJ3 crash row reads the app's own storage.
  - A pending-wipe flag kept in Preferences or Application Support would record, outside the user's file, that a removal happened and where the file is.
- **Fix.** Add "kept in the file itself (DF F58 (1))" to the note.

[INFO] **PL:183 (PM14-4 dogfood item).** It cites DJ3 (h), but (h) now lands the write before the crash, so no case produces "Your changes are saved" after a lost write. That is a claim about saving, not erasing, so it is out of my lens. Fix: re-point the cite.

F215, F61 and the two new pointer lines keep "at the first open at which that holds". The meaning is the same under F215's first sentence, and DFJ:55 pins the strict reading. Fix: align the wording at the next pass.

## Biggest privacy risks
1. **The app's own export or Save a copy holds the log copy silently (F211).** The only disclosure is the help-docs line at PL:198, which still needs the owner. PL:50's sub-run for it is not built yet.
2. **PRIV15-1.** A full volume can stall clearing the log with no stated retry, while E35's reason is stale.
3. **An orphaned log after a Finder move (PL:197, carried),** and the window between a crash and the reopen, when the log holds text and no notice shows.

## Genuinely privacy-respecting
- **(g) is anchored at the failure,** with a 10 s floor on room returning, so a build that waits for room now fails.
- **(h) requires E35 at the reopen** and a strict clearing deadline after it.
- **Each look reads the state before the bytes.** This keeps the one-way E35 check biased toward telling the user.
- **Rows and ADR input are honest about where removed text can survive.** R8.8, R6.2a and E35 are unchanged. The ADR input's crash clause takes the strict reading.
- **The main-file wipe succeeded on a full volume in my probe,** on both HFS+ and APFS images. I did not verify this with an APFS local snapshot; there the snapshot keeps the text regardless, and PL:195 discloses that.
- **No personal data in the Compare delta.** UJ5.3-r, UJ5.4-d, -f and -i, the accessibility row and the R5.4 copy trigger carry none.
- **"Your file won't keep what was there" (E8) is not an overstatement.** The delay is disclosed through E35 and the help docs.

[MAJOR] R15-M1 — DJ3 (a), and on the plain reading (b) and (f): DFJ:48, DFJ:49, DFJ:53 — the new look cadence has no start point, so looks taken before the delete lands fail a correct build
- **The change.** Round 13's (a) placed its first look "once the delete lands" (the diff's removed line). The rewrite replaced the fixed looks with "A look lists the state up and then takes a byte read…; looks run at least once a second" and says nowhere when looks begin.
- **What goes wrong.** Every row's When opens with "Let the delete land while read 1 runs", so looks that run with the When can come before the delete lands. (a)'s Result even qualifies its seeding read as "taken after the delete lands", which implies earlier looks exist.
  - Before the delete lands, the seeded committed log frame already holds the text beside the file (the fixture seeds it "before the delete"), and E35 is not up because nothing is pending.
  - (a)'s "while read 1 runs, E35 is up at each look" and its unconditional "at each look, a byte read finding the removed text beside the file finds E35 up" both fail on those looks.
  - (b)'s and (f)'s "until read 2 ends, at each look…" fail the same way, unless "removed text" is read as text already removed.
- **Mutation.** A harness that starts its once-a-second poller when the When begins marks a correct build red on the first look, before any wipe is pending. The fix for that red is a guess about when looks start.
- **Fix.** In each row's look sentence, write "looks run at least once a second from once the delete shows done". Starting at "shows done" also absorbs E35's render lag (R15-m6). In (a)'s Result, write "while read 1 runs after the delete lands, E35 is up at each look".

## Biggest risks (if executed as-is)
1. **R15-M1: (a) goes red on a correct build.** The first build phase against R6.2a fails for a harness that starts looking when the When begins, and a coding agent would then have to guess when looks start.
2. **R15-m2: the ADR-0003 "use" definition would contradict DJ3.** If ADR-0003 adopts the edited PL:169 wording literally, it demands a clearing that SQLite cannot perform, and DJ3 (b) and (h) contradict the ADR.
3. **R15-m1: an index-only reader would start R8.8.** The Status vocabulary still keeps a needs-discussion row out of in-progress, so the damage is limited.

## Plan strengths
- **DJ3 is now eight self-contained rows,** so the "As (x)" inheritance that produced a Major in each of rounds 12–14 is gone. Each row states its own actions and full Result, and (d) guards the seeding and (h)'s reopen.

  - In every configuration, the main file was clean within read 1's end and still clean before the reopen.

**(2) New Majors**

**[MAJOR] DB15-MAJOR-1: DJ3 (g)'s deadline, timed from the failure with the volume still full, fails a correct build on APFS about one run in six (DF journeys:54; post-lock.md:46; round-14 fixes file:16).**
- **Where.** (g)'s result: "within 5 s of the failure, a functional timeout, the volume still full, no file the app keeps beside the file holds the removed text, and E35 is not up".
- **The false premise.** post-lock.md:46 now calls the log copy under E15 "settled by F215 / DF F61, since clearing needs no room". The fixes file (:16) says TRUNCATE returned (0,0,0) with the volume still full "on HFS+ and APFS images". My round-14 probe said the same, but it used too few runs.
- **Reproduced on APFS (`probe_g15.py`, `probe_apfs_keep.py`).**
  - In 8 of 46 runs with the hold after SQLite's write lock, the held write failed with SQLITE_FULL, as it should.
  - The clearing then failed with SQLITE_IOERR_TRUNCATE on every one of its once-a-second retries for 5 s, and the WAL still held the marker.
  - Once room was restored, TRUNCATE returned (0,0,0).
  - HFS+ never failed (8 runs), and a raw `ftruncate` passed in one try.
  - This matches APFS's known behaviour on a 100%-full volume: freeing blocks needs copy-on-write metadata space.
- **A second counter-example to "needs no room" (`probe_room.py`).** It uses a fixture other than (g)'s:
  - a read begun before a delete holds the log;
  - committed writes grow the database past the main file;
  - the volume fills, then the read ends.

  PASSIVE and TRUNCATE both return SQLITE_FULL. The main file's wipe still lands, because pages are written in ascending order and the in-range pages come first, but the log keeps the removed text until room returns.
- **Integrity is unaffected.** integrity_check returned ok and no committed data was lost. Only the deadline is at stake.
- **Change that exposes it.** Run (g) on a real full APFS image, hold after the lock, about 20 times. Some runs fail although the build retries the clearing correctly.
- **Fix, without choosing a mechanism.** Change (g)'s result to: "E15 renders for the failed write; from the failure until room is restored, the volume still full, at each look a byte read finding the removed text beside the file finds E35 up at that look; within 5 s, a functional timeout, of room being restored, no file the app keeps beside the file holds it, and E35 is not up".
  - This still accepts a build that clears at the failure.
  - Reopen post-lock.md:46's E15 half as an owner item. F215/F61's "first moment" cannot be met through SQLite's truncation on a full APFS volume, or when frames not yet copied into the main file (not backfilled) must grow it. What should happen then: E35 stays up, and the log clears once room returns?
  - If the owner instead keeps the deadline at the failure, the case must declare "full" as fault injection on the app's writes only. That is a guess a builder cannot make today.

**[MAJOR] DB15-MAJOR-2: (g)'s "release the write, so that it fails and rolls back" is not guaranteed. A correct build with a small held write lands it on the full volume, so "E15 renders for the failed write" fails (DF journeys:54).**
- **Provenance.** This clause was carried into the rewritten row from round 13's (g), not introduced by it. My round-14 probe missed this path because it cleared eagerly.
- **The configuration.**
  - The hold sits before SQLite's write lock, a placement round 13 and 14 accepted.
  - The build defers its clearing until "no write runs", which F215 allows.
  - The held R8.1f/g write is a two-item bulk set.
- **Reproduced (`probe_g15.py`).** SQLite restarts the WAL at the write's start and overwrites its existing bytes in place. The COMMIT succeeds on the full volume in 5 of 5 runs across APFS and HFS+, with 2 rows set to Nova.
- **Change that exposes it.** Pair a deferred clearing with a hold placed before the lock and a held write smaller than the existing log.
- **Fix.** Add to (d)'s guard: "or a run of (g) whose released write lands rather than failing". Optionally, declare (g)'s held write large enough that it cannot fit in the log's existing length.

## Biggest risks
1. **(g) is a flaky gate on APFS, macOS's default filesystem.** It fails about 17% of correct runs, and in a deferred-clearing build with a small held write it fails every time. A team chasing the red will drift toward hacks such as zeroing the -wal file outside SQLite's locks, or toward a busy-wait.
2. **F215/F61's log deadline has a physical limit that no row states.** On a full APFS volume, or when frames not yet backfilled must grow the main file, the removed text stays in the log until room returns. E35 staying up is then the only honest outcome, and no row says so.
3. **Carried over from earlier rounds.** An outside reader left open keeps the log copy. The copied pages must reach stable storage (F_FULLFSYNC) before truncation, which is already an ADR-0003 note.

## Genuinely sound
- **The split into eight self-contained rows works.** No result clause is inherited. (e) and (f) still say "As in (b) until the held write lands", but that reuses only the action sequence, and each states its own result. That is correct, not a regression.
- **(h) is now the right test of F215's crash clause.** It fails a build that loses the pending wipe in the crash, which then never clears or drops E35 while the bytes remain. It also fails a build that treats a WAL restart as a clearing: in the "hold before the lock, read 2 at read-mark 0, deferred" configuration, the restart leaves the marker in the log's tail beyond the new frames.
- **The ADR input's "first such moment after reopening"** is the reading D69's "a read that spans a crash" intends. It removes the misreading "wait for a later open".
- **The full-volume failure is integrity-safe.** A failed TRUNCATE or checkpoint leaves integrity_check ok, with no committed row lost; only the wipe deadline slips.
- **UJ5.3-r and UJ5.4-d now declare decidable operands.** CX1 is spectral at D50/2°, and MR-001's current reading has an M1 value. So R5.4's order (can't-be-read, then no-value, then not-compared) is decidable from the file at SQLITE_READER_FLOOR. UJ5.3-q, which reuses UJ5.4-d's fixture, is now consistent.
- **The copy's R5.4 not-compared trigger** (CM copy:312) matches R5.4's "both having values" clause.

### Owner adjudication (2026-09-26)


The owner answered D72 on 2026-09-26, over round 15's database-lens DB15-MAJOR-1 (a full APFS volume stopping the log's truncation in 8 of 46 runs with SQLITE_IOERR_TRUNCATE; and, in both HFS+ and APFS, a clearing whose un-backfilled frames must grow the main file returning SQLITE_FULL) and the privacy lens's PRIV15-1 (the same growth case, reproduced independently). The record quotes the question, the option chosen with its description, and the option not chosen, verbatim.

**D72 (DB15-MAJOR-1, PRIV15-1).** Question: "When the disk is completely full, SQLite sometimes can't clear the log (about 1 run in 6 on APFS, and always if the log must grow the main file). Removed text then stays in the log beside your file until space frees up. E35 ('Saved — another app is reading your file…') is what the user sees meanwhile. What should the erase promise say for this case?" Chosen: **Clears when room returns** — "While a full volume stops the clearing, the log copy stays and E35 stays up. Within 5 s of room being restored the app clears it on its own, no user action needed. The rule's 'first moment' then reads '…and the volume has room to clear it'. Text in the main file itself is still wiped at its normal deadline." Not chosen: **Also stop new writes** — "Same, but while a clearing is stuck on a full disk the app starts no new write of its own, so nothing grows the log further. Stricter, but editing is blocked until you free space (on top of E15 already refusing writes that need room)."

## Biggest risks   (what builds the wrong thing or fails the user)
- **E35 is the only signal during a full-volume wait (PM16-1).** In the growth case it names the wrong cause and a remedy that doesn't work. The privacy promise still holds on its own, so this is a trust and wording risk, not data exposure. It must stay on the dogfood watch.
- **The give-way rule is implied, not stated (PM16-2).** The rejected blocking behavior is caught only by the fence's "Not chosen" text, not by any row or case.

## Genuinely solid   (incl. where simplicity is right that a product-zealot would over-spec)
- **D72's "no user action" auto-clear is right for the Cataloger.** Erasure never depends on the user understanding SQLite, and edits are not blocked on a full disk.
- **(g) is written by outcome, and (i) is the one forcing case.** That split is the right way to test a behavior that is non-deterministic on APFS: (g) tolerates it and (i) proves the retry.
- **(h)'s read-back of the landed write closes the round-14 concern** that E35 said "saved" at a reopen when nothing had been saved.
- **Not a finding:** a wait with no other app's read shows no E35. That silence is F211's settled own-reads clause.
- **README row 6's "not yet aligned" note is honest.** It tells a builder not to start R8.8 or R6.2a.

## Genuinely sound
- **Gating read 2 on clean bytes is a better fix than the one I proposed.** It removes the harness race, and it stops read 2 from deferring the main-file wipe. Per the architecture and plan probes, (h) stays exercised with read 2 begun after the copy-in.
- **Routing the full-volume case to the owner (D72) was right.** A tweak to the case would have hidden a physical limit. R6.2a's bound is a concrete owner-ratified 5 s, so it needs no named constant.
- **(i) is the right addition.** It is the realistic path: a long outside read plus captures grow the log until the disk is full. It pins the main-file wipe on a full volume, which PM N1, IF15-m4 and R15-m7 had asked for.
- **(d)'s guard for a (g) write that lands** turns DB15-MAJOR-2's false red into an honest "not exercised".
- **Not flagged:**
  - the raw "5 s" in R6.2a;
  - DF R6.2 moving to Ready for Alignment ahead of the lens dispositions, which is a recorded process call with a stated reason;
  - (e) and (f) spelling out their actions.

The crash is therefore gated on clean bytes by construction, and harness speed can no longer beat the app's wipe. `probe_h16.py A 0`: main file clean at +0.23 s; after the crash, "main holds text: False"; the landed write reads back after the reopen; TRUNCATE returns (1,3,2) while read 2 runs and (0,0,0) once it ends. |

**(2) New Major from the round-15 fixes**

[MAJOR] **TR16-1 — DF journeys:49 (b), :52 (e), :53 (f) and :55 (h): the new read-2 gate lets the removed text leave the log before or at the held write's landing, so the read-2 cases no longer test that a later read holds the log copy (F211/F212, R6.2a).**

- **The mechanism.** Once the main file is clean, the log is fully copied in, and read 2 begins at SQLite's read-mark 0. A read at mark 0 blocks copying further frames into the main file. It blocks neither of these:
  - **A clearing before the landing.** If the build clears eagerly and the hold sits before SQLite's write lock, TRUNCATE succeeds as soon as the main file is clean. `probe_h16_eager.py B 6`: "main clean at +0.22s; log holds text: False", before read 2 even begins.
  - **A log restart at the landing.** If the build clears late, a held write that starts its SQLite transaction only at release begins on a fully copied-in log. Its commit then restarts the log and overwrites it from the first frame.
    - `probe_h16.py B 0`, with the text in the log's first frame as the natural seeding puts it: "landed (1, 1, 0); after landing: log holds text: False", and TRUNCATE is still busy. The text left through SQLite's restart, not through the build's clearing.
    - `probe_h16.py B 6`, with the text frame later in the log: the text survives and stays pinned.
- **Round 14's order pinned the text in every configuration.** There, read 2 began before the wipe, at a nonzero mark. `probe_h16_oldorder.py B 0` returns (1,3,2) and `probe_h16_oldorder_eager.py B 6` returns (1,20,19), with the text kept in both.
- **Which builds this affects.** Holding the write before SQLite's write lock is a placement rounds 13–14 accepted (see DB15-MAJOR-2). R8.10a (CM PRD:454) does not fix the hold's placement. (d) at :51 reports this only for (h), and only after the reopen. It has no guard for (b), (e) or (f).
- **Mutations that pass (b), (e) and (f) with that placement and first-frame seeding:**
  - **W-F211:** the build treats only reads begun before the wipe as holding the log, so it drops E35 when the held write lands while read 2 runs.
  - **W-F212:** the build tries the clearing once when the held write lands and never again when a read ends. This is SSE14-1's build.
- **What those builds do in the field.** In real use, the text's frame can lie beyond the frames the write overwrites, or a read may hold a nonzero mark. Both builds then leave the removed text beside the file, either with E35 down or past R6.2a's first moment.
- **The same builds fail (b) under `probe_h16.py A`,** where the hold sits after SQLite's write lock.
- **(h) is affected too.** For these builds it is always reported not exercised, so F58 (1) after a crash is never checked.
- **Fix, in the journeys only, with no PRD words:**
  - In the journal-or-log fixture that (a) declares and (b)–(i) restate, add: the held write is "held only once it has begun writing to the file, before read 1 ends". This blocks both the early clearing and the restart. It also makes (g)'s write fail rather than land, which was DB15-MAJOR-2's root cause.
  - Add to (d): "a run of (b), (e) or (f) whose first byte read after the held write lands finds the removed text beside the file nowhere" reports not exercised.
  - Do not revert the gate. It correctly stops read 2 being "a read begun before its wipe" under R6.2a (R15-m5, ARCH15-9).

**Minors (post-lock, one line each)**
- [MINOR] DF journeys:51/:56 — (i) has no not-exercised guard for a run whose log copy is gone before room is restored (for example, the ≥ 1 MB write reuses free pages so nothing grows). A build with no room-return retry then passes (i), which is F218's only deterministic carrier.
- [MINOR] DF journeys:56 — (i) never asserts that E15 stays down. A build that maps the clearing's SQLITE_FULL to E15 ("your last change wasn't saved") passes even though the change landed.
- [MINOR] DF journeys:56 — (i)'s main-file clause needs a declared-full state in which in-place overwrites succeed. That rule lives only at post-lock:169 (ARCH15-8), so a harness that makes every write fail would fail a correct build. Cite it in (i).
- [MINOR] DF journeys:56 — "adds at least 1 MB of new rows" fits no clear P0 R8.1f/g write, since a bulk set grows existing rows. Say "adds at least 1 MB to the file's stored content".

## Biggest risks   (what could ship broken behind a green suite)
- **TR16-1.** Suppose a build places the R8.10a hold before SQLite's write lock and gets F211 or F212 wrong. It passes all of DJ3's read-2 cases, and (h) never runs. It then ships:
  - with E35 down while removed text sits beside the file; or
  - with the log copy outliving a later read's end until the next write or open.
- **(i)'s missing guard.** If the growth precondition silently fails, F218's room-return retry ships untested, because (g) under the declared-full hook clears as soon as E15 renders.
- **m6.** A stray "From current" label next to Compare's slot stays green.

## Genuinely solid   (incl. where minimal scoping is correct that a coverage-zealot would wrongly flag)
- **TR15-1's fix is exact.** The clean-bytes gate now sits upstream of the crash, so the harness-speed race is gone (`probe_h16.py A`).
- **(g) under D72 is correctly minimal.** Asserting a clearing at E15 would fail correct builds 8 times in 46 on APFS. The one-way E35 check plus the room-return deadline is the only oracle that holds on every run, and (d) covers a write that lands.
- **(h) is stronger.**
  - It now asserts that the landed write reads back after the reopen, which kills a build that discards the log file at open.
  - Its E35 check starts from the opening state, which removes the look-while-opening race.
- **(i) works whatever the hold placement.** Read 1 stops the log restarting, and the growth makes the clearing fail with the volume full. It deterministically kills a build with no room-return retry and a build that drops E35 when read 1 ends. The probe evidence from the database and architecture lenses (probe_room.py, probe15_growth.py) shows the main file still comes out clean.
- **Untouched cases.** UJ2.1-g, UJ2.3-a/b, UJ3.3-n/o, UJ3.4-m/n, UJ5.3-b/o/p, UJ5.4-c/d and UJ7.1-u are not in this diff and stand as round 15 found them.

[MAJOR] **IF16-1 — DJ3 (g) at DFJ:54 against DF R6.2a (DF:228) and F218; also PL:46.** (g) now passes a build that postpones every clearing while the volume is full, and no case catches it.
- **What the contract says.** R6.2a's D72 clause applies only "where a full volume stops that clearing". F218's first bullet says the same. Where truncation succeeds on a full volume, the normal "first moment" deadline still applies. The owner's own question assumed that: "SQLite *sometimes* can't clear the log".
- **What changed in (g).**
  - Old (17de231): "within 5 s of the failure, … the volume still full, no file … holds the removed text, and E35 is not up".
  - New: only the one-way E35 check, then "within 5 s of room being restored … no file … holds the removed text".
- **Traced by hand, under the declared-full hook PL:169 already requires ("writes that allocate fail, while truncation and in-place overwrites succeed", ARCH15-8):**
  - A correct build clears when the write fails, well within 5 s. It passes.
  - The mutation: gate the clearing on "the volume is not full". That build keeps the copy for at least 10 s, E35 up, and clears when room returns. It also passes the new (g), and it failed the old (g).
  - (i), at DFJ:56, forces growth, so it cannot tell these two builds apart either. No other case combines a full volume with a log copy. I searched both journeys files.
- **Three texts now read the rule the wrong way:**
  - PL:46's new wording: "the log copy stays, E35 up, until room returns", with no condition.
  - The literal reading of F218's third bullet and F62's "'first moment' reads '…and the volume has room to clear it'" (CMf:1871, DFf:687).
  - (g)'s acceptance of both behaviours.

  So a builder can choose between "try the clearing, fall back to waiting" and "wait whenever the volume is full". The second leaves removed text in the log for the whole full period, even in the 38 of 46 APFS runs, and every HFS+ run, where it could have been cleared.
- **Fix (does not reopen D72):**
  1. In (g)'s action, pin what the declared-full state lets through: "declare the volume full (R7.3), a declared-full state in which a write that needs new space fails and a truncation or in-place overwrite succeeds". This is the post-lock hook ARCH15-8 already names, and it removes the APFS flakiness DB15-MAJOR-1 found.
  2. Restore (g)'s old assertion: "within 5 s of E15 rendering, a functional timeout, the volume still full, no file the app keeps beside the file holds the removed text and E35 is not up".
  3. Keep (i) as the D72 case: the clearing is stopped, the copy stays, and it clears within 5 s of room returning.
  4. Make PL:46 conditional: "where the full volume stops the clearing".
  5. Add an orchestrator Clarified line under F218 and under F62: "room to clear it" means room enough for that clearing to succeed.
  6. If the orchestrator reads D72 as "wait whenever the volume is full", that is a question for the owner, not an edit.

## Verdict
**Sound: build it.** Both of my round-15 Majors are resolved at `74f058b`, and the round-15 fixes add no new Blocker or Major. What remains is seven Minors and five Nits for post-lock. The most useful of them comes from a new probe: a full APFS volume can stop the main-file wipe from being saved to disk (ARCH16-4). No DJ3 case fails because of it.

## Architecture in brief
- **Who owns what.** Data Foundation owns the file, the erase lifecycle, E35 and the one-writer rule (R1.11). CM R8.8 hands the journal-or-log copy to DF R6.2a, and ADR-0003 owns the mechanism.
- **Two deadlines.** Text in the main file is wiped at the read-based deadline (F200/F202). The log copy goes at F215's first moment.
- **What D72 adds (F218/F62).** Where a full volume stops the clearing, the copy stays, E35 stays up, and the app clears it within 5 s of room returning.
- **Tradeoff, unchanged.** Writes never wait on reads, the log copy trails behind, and E35 discloses it. WAL is forced by the ADR input's non-waiting save, not by these rows.
- **Subject.** `git diff 17de231 74f058b -- docs ':!docs/agent-reviews'`, with every cited line read at `74f058b`.
- **Working tree.** It carries uncommitted round-16 edits in 9 files (DFJ:51/54/56, DF:228, CM:446, ADRQ:22, CMF after F218, DFF after F62, PL:46/183). I did not review them as the subject. They appear to address ARCH16-1, ARCH16-2, ARCH16-3 and the first, second and fourth Nits.

**Minors and Nits (post-lock, one line each)**
- **[MINOR] ARCH16-1 — (g) (DFJ:54) with R6.2a (DF:228).** (g) never defines "where a full volume stops that clearing", so it passes a build that suspends all clearing after any SQLITE_FULL until room returns. That build is wrong whenever the declared-full state lets truncation succeed (PL:169's ARCH15-8 hook), because the clearing was never stopped. Fix: state the hook's behaviour in (g) and assert the clearing within 5 s of E15 rendering.
- **[MINOR] ARCH16-2 — (d) (DFJ:51) and (i) (DFJ:56).** There is no not-exercised guard for an (i) run whose log is clean before room returns. For example, the 1 MB write may reuse freelist pages the delete freed, so nothing grows. Such a run passes a build that never retries after SQLITE_FULL. Fix: add that guard.
- **[MINOR] ARCH16-3 — (i) (DFJ:56).** Nothing asserts E15. A build that raises E15 ("your last change wasn't saved", DFF:627 (3)) for the failed clearing shows a false state and passes. Fix: assert that E15 does not render.
- **[MINOR] ARCH16-4 — F218's "Text in the main file is still wiped at its normal deadline" (CMF:1872) and (i)'s main-file clause (DFJ:56).** The storage cannot make this wipe durable when the file shares disk blocks with an APFS clone.
  - PROBE, raw write: an in-place write plus fsync on a full volume succeeded 3/3 on a plain file and failed ENOSPC 3/3 on a file cloned with `/bin/cp -c`.
  - PROBE, SQLite on a cloned file (4 runs): PASSIVE and TRUNCATE failed with SQLITE_IOERR_FSYNC. A byte read found the main file clean while mounted. After detach and re-attach, still full, the removed text was back in the main file. The `-wal` still held the delete's frames.
  - Control: the same growth case on an unshared file stayed clean across detach and re-attach.
  - Where it bites: Finder Duplicate, a clone-based copy should ADR-0003 choose one, or a Time Machine local snapshot (the snapshot case is unprobed; it uses the same copy-on-write mechanism). A byte-read oracle cannot see this, and the ARCH15-8 hook ("in-place overwrites succeed") hides it.
  - Fix, not re-litigating D72: an ADR-0003 note that a wipe whose sync fails for want of room is handled like F218's stopped clearing. That falls out if E35 and the retry are tied to the log clearing succeeding, since SQLite syncs the main file before it truncates. Also record that the hook does not model shared blocks.
- **[MINOR] ARCH16-5 — R6.2a's D72 clause (DF:228).** "Within 5 s of room returning, its clearing then running before the next write starts" is met only if the pending clearing is attempted at each write start as well as by a poll. With a poll alone, a long R8.1f/g write begun between room returning and the poll holds the clearing past 5 s. Needs an ADR-0003 note.
- **[MINOR] ARCH16-6 — every "within 5 s" wipe deadline.**
  - macOS gives the app no signal when free space returns or when another app's read ends, so these deadlines depend on a background poll.
  - App Nap can throttle that poll when the app is not frontmost; the only mention of App Nap in the docs is a named gap in the Rust research results.
  - D72's pending state can last hours, which makes this worse. The engineering plan should hold an activity assertion while any wipe or clearing is pending.
- **[MINOR] ARCH16-7 — the pending-wipe marker (PL:169, ARCH15-6).** Under D72 a pending clearing can outlive a close or crash while the volume is full, and a full volume refuses the marker's own write. So the marker must be written with, or before, the text-removing write, not when the deferral is first noticed. No DJ3 row crashes while the volume is full.
- **[NIT] ADRQ:22.** "and where a full volume stops that clearing within 5 s of room returning" lacks R6.2a's commas and can parse as the condition. Its inline parenthetical still cites only F211/F212/F215 and F60/F61.
- **[NIT] CM:446.** R8.8 cites "F59–F61" where "F59–F62" is a word-neutral swap.
- **[NIT] DFF:673–678.** F61 has no Clarified pointer to F62, while CMF:1847 points F215 to F218.
- **[NIT] DF:228.** "that clearing" has no antecedent until "its clearing" later in the same sentence.
- **[NIT] Stacked pointer lines.** To assemble the log rule a builder reads F200 → F202 → F211 → F212 → F215 → F218, with pointer lines under four fences. Name R6.2a and ADRQ:22 as the consolidated statement.

## Biggest risks
- **The full-volume path is tested only through a declared-full hook.** Real APFS differs in two ways the hook does not show:
  - truncation fails in about 1 run in 6 (the database lens's round-15 probe);
  - pages written in place to a file that shares blocks with a clone never reach disk (ARCH16-4).

  D72's defer-and-retry covers both, but only if ADR-0003 ties E35 and the retry to the clearing actually succeeding.
- **The pending-wipe marker is a schema-level one-way door.** It now also has to survive a full volume (ARCH16-7).
- **The deadlines depend on background polling that nothing owns** (ARCH16-5, ARCH16-6).

## Genuinely sound
- **Both round-15 fixes are minimal and correct.** (h) is gated on clean bytes. D72 plus (i) turn a physical limit into a stated, testable outcome, with no PRD words beyond R6.2a's clause.
- **D72's rejected "Also stop new writes" was the right call.** On a full volume a log append needs new space and fails on its own with E15. In the growth state SQLite cannot restart the log. Blocking writes would add a mode and no protection.
- **The rows stay storage-neutral.** In rollback-journal DELETE mode the journal is unlinked at each commit, so D72 holds trivially.
- **One source of truth.** R8.8 delegates to R6.2a, and ADRQ:22 mirrors it without naming a checkpoint mode. "Within 5 s of room returning" is a behaviour, not a mechanism.
- **(i) is well built.** The main-file bytes are clean even though the checkpoint fails, because pages inside the file are copied in place first (PROBE 3/3). The file stays clean across an unmount when no clone shares its blocks.
- **The DJ3 set now holds together.** Each of (a)–(i) has its own action sequence and result. With the shared look start point and read 2 gated on clean bytes, the timing guesses behind rounds 12–15 are gone.

## Verdict
**Privacy-sound to ship.** D72 closes PRIV15-1, and the round-15 fixes bring in no new Critical or High. Two Mediums and two Lows go to post-lock, all on disclosure or case strength. None is in R8.8's or R6.2a's own text.

## Data-flow & PII map (brief)
- **Data subjects:** the Cataloger, and anyone named in notes, swatch names, collection names or imported free text. None of it is special-category. The delta adds no personal field, no store and no egress.
- **Where removed text survives:**
  - **Main file:** until reads begun before the wipe have ended. F218 keeps this deadline on a full volume, and DJ3 (i) tests it.
  - **The log beside the file:** until the first moment, with the file open, that no read uses it and no write runs. New under D72: where a full volume stops that clearing, until room returns, plus 5 s.
  - **Outside the promise:** R5.8's copies, Save a copy, exports and backups.
- **Disclosure:**
  - E35 shows for another app's read and stays up through a full-volume stall.
  - Nothing shows for the app's own export or Save a copy (F211). Nothing shows for a stall that follows one, or for a stall that spans a close and reopen.
- **Readers of a log copy:** sync clients, backups, and copies of the folder.

[MEDIUM] **PRIV16-1 — DFJ:54 (g), with PL:46: (g) now passes the mutation PRIV14-1 closed.**
- **The problem.** Re-timed to room's return, (g) accepts a build that suspends every clearing while the volume is full.
- **What R6.2a and F218 require.** DF:228 and CMF:1871 clear at the failure, unless the full volume actually stops the clearing.
- **Why it is never stopped in (g).** In (g), the clearing is an in-place copy back plus a truncation.
  - Under the declared-full hook PL:169 now specifies (ARCH15-8: truncation and in-place overwrites succeed), that is never stopped.
  - It is also never stopped on HFS+, and not in about 5 of 6 runs on real APFS (DB15-MAJOR-1).
- **Mutation.** Gate the clearing on "the volume has room". It passes (g) today.
- **PL:46.** It states the same unconditional reading: "the log copy stays, E35 up, until room returns".
- **Why Medium, not High as in round 14.**
  - The extra retention is removed text beside the file for the whole full-disk period, where the correct build keeps none.
  - E35 stays up throughout, though its reason is stale.
  - That is the kind of retention D72 accepted for a stopped clearing.
- **Fix.**
  - Declare the volume full through the hook in (g), and assert "within 5 s of E15 rendering, no file the app keeps beside the file holds the removed text and E35 is not up". Leave the stopped path to (i).
  - Scope PL:46 to "where a full volume stops that clearing".
  - (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), storage limitation.)

[MEDIUM] **PRIV16-2 — CMF:1869 and DFF:687: "E35 stays up" assumes E35 is already up.**
- **Why it may not be.** F211 (CMF:1802) raises E35 only for another app's read.
- **Two silent cases.** In each, removed text stays beside the file with no notice until room returns and the file is open:
  - A stall after the app's own export or Save a copy. A long read of the app's own is exactly what grows the log until the disk fills.
  - Any stall that spans a close, quit and reopen. E35 goes with the file, and F58 (1) shows it again only while another app reads.
- **User-facing text that then overstates:**
  - E35's "or when you next open the file" (DFC:30).
  - The bulk-edit confirmation's "Your file won't keep what was there" (CMC:127, CMC:129).
  - R1.5's help-docs clause (DF:103) and PL:195–198, which name reading elsewhere and exports but never a full disk.
- **Fix (post-lock; costs no body words).**
  - Help docs: "If your disk is full, text you removed or replaced can stay in a file beside yours until you free space; SpectroCapture then wipes it on its own the next time the file is open."
  - A Clarified line under F218 and F62: "raises no E35 where none is up (F211)".
  - Add DJ3 (i)'s window (E35 up, no E15, no app reading) to PL:183's dogfood item.
  - (GDPR Art. 5(1)(a) and Art. 12, transparency.)

[LOW] **PRIV16-3 — DF:228, the D72 clause read as a stand-alone deadline.**
- **The problem.** "Or, where a full volume stops that clearing, within 5 s of room returning" reads as its own deadline. F218's third bullet (CMF:1871) makes it conditional on the first moment: file open, no read, no write.
- **Consequences.**
  - Read literally, it cannot be met when a read holds the log, or the app is closed, as room returns.
  - It nudges a builder toward a background watcher that records the file's path outside the file, against DF F58 (1).
  - No DJ3 row exercises either case, so no case fails today.
- **Fix.** A Clarified line: "…the file open and nothing else holding the log; otherwise at the first such moment after; the log itself is the only marker (DF F58 (1))."

[LOW] **PRIV16-4 — DFJ:51 (d) has no guard for (i) (DFJ:56).**
- **The problem.** A run where the log is already clean just before room is restored passes (i) without exercising D72's retry.
- **Fix.** Add to (d): "…or a run of (i) whose last byte read before room is restored finds the removed text beside the file nowhere".

## Biggest privacy risks
1. **PRIV16-2:** a silent full-volume stall after the app's own export, or across a reopen, while the copy promises the text is gone.
2. **PRIV16-1:** a build that holds the log copy for the whole full-disk period passes (g).
3. **Carried from earlier rounds:**
   - the app's own export holds the log copy silently (PL:198, still needs the owner);
   - the window between a crash and the reopen;
   - an orphaned log after a Finder move (PL:197).

## Genuinely privacy-respecting
- **D72 keeps the main-file wipe at its normal deadline on a full volume, and (i) tests it.** A build that leaves main-file text until room returns fails.
- **(i) tests the retry.** Room returns at least 10 s after read 1 ends, against a 5 s deadline, so a build without a retry fails.
- **The full-volume exception is in R6.2a's own text, not hidden in a fence.** README:18 also says plainly that R8.8 and R6.2/R6.2a are not yet aligned.
- **(h) crashes only once the main file is clean.** It asserts E35 from the opening state after the reopen.
- **Declining "Also stop new writes" costs no privacy.**
  - Writes that need room already fail with E15.
  - In-place writes do not keep the text past room's return.
- **The UJ2.3-d edit and the R5.4 flip carry no personal data.**

**(2) New Majors introduced by the round-15 fixes**

[MAJOR] R16-M1 — DJ3 (g) (DFJ:54), with PL:46 and PL:169 — under the declared-full test hook this pass wrote into PL:169, (g)'s clearing is only a truncation and is never stopped, yet (g) now asserts only F218's "within 5 s of room being restored". A build that keeps the log copy whenever the volume reads full passes (g) and (i), although F215 and F218 require it to clear at the first moment.

- **What changed.**
  - Before round 15, (g) asserted that the copy was gone "within 5 s of the failure, the volume still full".
  - Under D72 the orchestrator rewrote (g) so that the copy may stay "from then until room is restored" and must be gone "within 5 s of room being restored".
  - The same pass added ARCH15-8 to PL:169: "the declared-full test hook must behave like a real full volume, writes that allocate failing while truncation and in-place overwrites succeed".
- **Why (g) can never reach F218's branch.** (g) declares the volume full only "once a look finds the file's own bytes clean". At that point every committed frame is already copied into the main file, so the clearing is a pure truncation.
  - Under the ARCH15-8 hook, that truncation succeeds.
  - The architecture lens's round-15 control (log line 24684) and the database lens's HFS+ runs (log line 25037) show the same on a real HFS+ volume: TRUNCATE returned (0,0,0) with the volume still full.
  - So at E15 there is no read, no write, and the volume has room to clear the log. That is F215's first moment as F218 qualifies it (FN:1871; DFF:687), and the correct build clears within 5 s of E15.
  - F218 keeps the copy only "where a full volume stops the clearing" (FN:1869). Under the hook, that never happens in (g). Only (i), the growth case, stops it.
- **What goes wrong.**
  - (g) accepts both the correct build and a build that holds the copy until room returns.
  - (i) cannot tell the two apart either, because the clearing really is stopped there.
  - PL:46 now summarises the rule as unconditional: "the log copy stays, E35 up, until room returns, then clears within 5 s (DJ3 (g), (i))". That drops F218's condition, so an ADR-0003 author reading post-lock would build the wrong behaviour.
  - F218's Carried-by field names (g) as a carrier (FN:1874), but under the hook (g) cannot exercise F218's branch.
- **Mutation.** Gate the clearing loop on free space (statfs f_bavail > 0), or skip clearing while E15 is up and retry only once room returns. Today (a)–(i) all stay green. Under the fix below, (g) goes red.
- **Fix (journeys and post-lock only, no PRD words).**
  - Make (g) the full-volume case where only a truncation remains:
    - its When reads "declare the volume full (R7.3), writes that allocate failing while truncation and in-place overwrites succeed";
    - its Result reads "within 5 s of E15 rendering, a functional timeout, the volume still declared full, no file the app keeps beside the file holds the removed text and E35 is not up; until then, at each look, a byte read finding the removed text beside the file finds E35 up at that look";
    - it cites F61 and F215 (with F211 for E15).
  - Leave F218's stopped-clearing branch to (i). Change F218's and F62's Carried-by and the F218 map line to "(i)".
  - Rewrite PL:46 as "…where only a truncation remains, the copy clears at the first moment (F215 / DF F61; DJ3 (g)). Where a full volume stops the clearing — frames not yet copied in that would grow the file, or a truncation the volume refuses — it stays, E35 up, until room returns, then clears within 5 s (F218 / DF F62, D72; DJ3 (i))".

**(2) New Majors**

**[MAJOR] DB16-MAJOR-1 — R6.2a's D72 clause and the ADR-0003 input set a hard 5 s deadline that SQLite cannot meet while a read uses the log (DF PRD:228; decisions/README.md:22).**
- **The text.**
  - R6.2a: "…that no read uses that journal or log and no write runs, or, where a full volume stops that clearing, within 5 s of room returning, its clearing then running…".
  - The ADR input: "…and where a full volume stops that clearing within 5 s of room returning,…". It also lacks the commas, so it can be read as "stops that clearing within 5 s".
  - Both make the 5 s an alternative deadline of its own.
- **The fence says otherwise.** F218's Decision (CM fences:1871; DF fences:687) makes room a third condition on the first moment: F215's "first moment" reads "…and the volume has room to clear it". The row keeps the fence's 5 s bullet and drops this one.
- **Where it bites: the growth case's natural sequel.** A sync client re-reads the file after it changes.
- **Probe (`probe_reader_at_room.py`, HFS+).**
  - Read 1 ends on the full volume. PASSIVE and TRUNCATE both return SQLITE_FULL; the main file is clean and the -wal holds the text.
  - A new outside read (read 3) begins while the volume is full, and then room is restored.
  - TRUNCATE copies every frame back, returning (1,308,308), but stays busy at every attempt from room's return through 6.1 s. The -wal still holds the text.
  - Only after read 3 ends does it return (0,0,0) with the -wal clean. integrity_check is ok.
- **What a correct build faces.** It waits for read 3 and misses the row's literal deadline. The only way to meet the text is to truncate the -wal outside SQLite's locks, which breaks read 3's snapshot. No DJ3 row has a read spanning room's return, so the builder has to guess which reading governs.
- **Change that exposes it.** Add to (i) a read 3, begun after read 1 ends and before room is restored, and ended no sooner than 10 s after room returns. The literal R6.2a text then fails every correct build.
- **Fix (+3 words; DF is at 8,445 of 8,450).**
  - In R6.2a, replace "log and no write runs, or, where a full volume stops that clearing, within 5 s of room returning," with "log, no write runs and the volume has room to clear it (within 5 s of room returning, when room comes last),".
  - Mirror it in the ADR-0003 input, which also fixes the garden path.

**Minors and Nits (for post-lock, one line each)**
- **[MINOR] m1 — the declared-full hook at post-lock.md:169 skips D72's own trigger.** It pins "truncation and in-place overwrites succeed", which ARCH15-8 wrote for the pre-D72 (g). Under D72, a correct build run on that hook clears at E15, so no DJ3 row exercises SQLITE_IOERR_TRUNCATE (or SQLITE_IOERR_FSYNC, see m2). A build that retries a clearing on SQLITE_FULL but treats SQLITE_IOERR_* as fatal passes both (g) and (i). Fix: give the hook a variant in which truncation and fsync fail while the volume is declared full, run (g) in it, and add to (d) "a run of (g) whose first look after E15 finds the removed text beside the file nowhere". The uncommitted (g) rewrite in the worktree pins the opposite; I have not reviewed it.
- **[MINOR] m2 — new evidence on F218's "main file still wiped at its normal deadline" (`probe_clone_wipe.py`, APFS).** This records a storage limit; it does not re-open D72.
  - The setup: the file shares its blocks with an APFS clone. Finder's Duplicate makes one, and so does `FileManager.copyItem`, which clones on APFS by default — including an R5.8 snapshot or Save a copy made that way.
  - On a full volume, PASSIVE returns SQLITE_IOERR_FSYNC, and a byte read finds the main file clean because the pages sit only in the page cache.
  - After a remount, the removed text is back in the main file. In the raw test, 256 of 256 pages reverted.
  - When the text lived only in the main file, no log copy keeps E35 up.
  - Integrity is ok. The log keeps the delete's frames, so the first checkpoint with room wipes the pages again, durably.
  - For the owner and ADR-0003: have the app make its copies without cloning, and treat IOERR_FSYNC as a full-volume stop. Time Machine local snapshots share blocks the same way, though macOS purges them under space pressure.
- **[MINOR] m3 — (i)'s fixture wording (DF journeys:56).** "Adds at least 1 MB of new rows" fits few R8.1f/g writes: set, clear and reorder update rows, a delete removes them, and only E10's Undo, a P1 feature, inserts. State the growth itself: "whose committed frames would grow the file at least 1 MB past its own end". Also add to (d) "a run of (i) whose first look after read 1's end finds the removed text beside the file nowhere", for a file whose free pages absorbed the write.
- **[MINOR] m4 — (g) can go unexercised (DF journeys:51/54).** With a deferred clearing and a hold placed before the lock, (g)'s small write always lands, so (g) always reports not exercised. Give (g)'s held write (i)'s at-least-1 MB size, so every correct build fails the write and exercises (g).
- **[MINOR] m5 — the pending-wipe marker needs an ordering (post-lock.md:169, ARCH14-4).** It must commit in the delete's own transaction and be cleared only after the log's truncation, and its F_FULLFSYNC, have returned. If it is cleared first, a crash in between leaves text beside the file with no marker, and (h)'s E35 check at the reopen fails.
- **[MINOR] m6 — F218 presupposes E35 is already up.** "E35 stays up" does not cover a clearing that a full volume stops when no read ever deferred it. Example: the delete's own frames take the last free blocks, then APFS truncation fails. The text then sits beside the file with no state shown.
- **[NIT] R8.8 (CM PRD:446)** still cites the Data Foundation's "F59–F61"; it should be F59–F62. This is word-neutral, and the uncommitted worktree already has it.
- **[NIT] UJ2.3-d (CM journeys:241).** "Only the column stored State changed, among TT-001's and TT-002's stored values" fails a correct build if ADR-0003 keeps a per-item modified time. Scope it to "their imported and measurement values".

## Biggest risks
1. **The literal R6.2a deadline (DB16-MAJOR-1).** A builder chasing "within 5 s of room returning" while a sync client still reads the file has one way to "meet" it: truncating the -wal outside SQLite's locks. That corrupts the reader's snapshot.
2. **Clone-shared blocks on a full APFS volume (m2).** The main-file wipe is then only in the page cache, and the text returns after a power loss. Swift's default copy API creates exactly this sharing.
3. **The pinned hook tests only SQLITE_FULL (m1).** The clearing's retry also has to treat IOERR_TRUNCATE and IOERR_FSYNC as a full volume, and no case forces that today.

## Genuinely sound
- **(g) under D72 is deliverable.** It checks E35 one way while the volume is full and times the clearing from room's return; my round-15 APFS probe had TRUNCATE returning (0,0,0) once room was restored.
- **(i)'s main-file clause is deliverable.** A checkpoint copies pages in ascending order, so pages within the file's current length land before the first page that needs the file to grow fails. Re-confirmed this round: the main file is clean while PASSIVE and TRUNCATE return SQLITE_FULL.
- **Every full-volume failure path is integrity-safe.** SQLITE_FULL, IOERR_TRUNCATE and IOERR_FSYNC each leave integrity_check ok and lose no committed row. SQLite does not advance its count of copied frames, so the first checkpoint with room repairs the state.
- **The DJ3 action fixes are right.**
  - Gating read 2 on clean bytes in (b), (e), (f) and (h) removes F57's "read begun before the wipe" ambiguity.
  - Gating (h)'s crash the same way removes the timing race.
  - (h)'s readback of the landed write fails a build that discards the -wal.
- **PL:169's "no write has committed since it began" is correct in SQLite's terms.** A reader on READ_LOCK(0) blocks copying later frames into the file.
- **Correct choices a textbook DBA might wrongly flag:**
  - E35 standing in during a full volume, and not stopping new writes (both D72);
  - a (d) "not exercised" guard rather than dictating where the hold sits;
  - nine self-contained rows.

  - (g)'s write size;
  - a copy-without-cloning note for ADR-0003;
  - the marker's commit and clear ordering.
- **Over-engineered:** nothing.

[MAJOR] **SSE17-1 — DFJ:56 (i): the new edit's E15 assumes a log with no leftover space, and (d) (DFJ:51) has no guard for an edit that lands.**
- **The row.** (i) runs in "the declared-full state (g) states", in which an in-place overwrite succeeds. It then asserts "for the edit E15 renders within 1 s … the edit never shown disabled and no write's progress showing".
- **What the fixture sizes.** It sizes only the bulk write, by main-file growth: "grow the file at least 1 MB past its own end". It says nothing about space left in the log past its last frame.
- **Where the leftover space comes from.** A log restart during seeding keeps the `-wal` at its old length, unless the build sets `journal_size_limit`. This is the same effect PL:172 already records for UJ6.2-g. The fixture's "enough items" makes a large, auto-checkpointed seeding log likely.
- **What a correct build does.** In the growth state the log cannot restart, so the edit's frame goes on at the last committed frame. If that point is inside the `-wal`'s existing length, the write is an in-place overwrite and it lands.
  - That is D72's chosen behaviour: the not-chosen option at CMF:1869 reads "on top of E15 already refusing writes that need room", and the Clarified line at CMF:1878 reads "editing is never blocked on it".
  - The correct build therefore shows the edit done, with no E15, and fails (i).
- **Mutation that passes: Build R.**
  - While a clearing is stuck, R refuses every write with E15 without trying it. This is the not-chosen "Also stop new writes", surfaced as E15 rather than as a disabled control.
  - R renders E15 within 1 s, never shows the edit disabled and shows no progress, so it passes (i) in every harness.
  - It is also the "fix" a builder reaches for when the false red above appears.
- **Why this counts as a Major.** The round-16 diff added this clause. Under a fixture the row allows, a correct build fails it, and the row rewards the rejected option. This is the same class as R16-M2, which the orchestrator confirmed for (g). The (i) edit was my own SSE16-m6 proposal, and I missed the leftover-space dependency.
- **Fix (journeys only, no PRD words):**
  1. In (i)'s Given, add "the log holding no space past its last frame once the write lands, so that the edit's frame needs new space and on the full volume fails". The recipe is PL:172's "log truncated to zero" before seeding.
  2. Add to (d): "a run of (i) whose edit lands rather than failing".
  3. For post-lock: add a positive case in which an edit that fits the log's existing length lands and shows done while the clearing is stuck. That is the only case that fails Build R.
